A reduced-order model balancing accuracy and complexity is established, and a decoupled equivalent damping analysis method is proposed to quantitatively characterize the stability of the dominant GFL and GFM oscillation modes from the perspective of damping formation mechanism. It is found that the GFL-dominated and GFM-dominated oscillation modes exhibit opposite stability evolution trends with respect to grid strength and are constrained by the dual-source power coupling effect. As a result, a single fixed parameter set cannot ensure stable system operation across a wide range of grid strengths and full power operating conditions. Furthermore, the influence of key control parameters on the oscillation modes is clarified, and stable parameter boundaries under extreme operating conditions are determined. Time-domain simulations validate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis and the proposed stable domain construction method.

title: Graph Neural Network With Dual-Stream Attention for Global Maximum Power Point Tracking Under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: Due to the complex nonlinear coupling between circuit topology and environmental changes, precise maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions remains a challenge. Existing data-driven methods typically view photovoltaic (PV) arrays as unstructured feature vectors or Euclidean grids, which fail to capture the fundamental series-parallel constraints that control the distribution of current and voltage. This study proposes a graph neural network with dual-stream attention (GNN-DSA), which is a physical perception framework that can strictly decouple static topologies from dynamic environmental signals. Static streams encode arrays into message-passed directed graphs with specific edge types that capture series-parallel circuit constraints, while dynamic streams capture irradiation patterns through the Transformer. A novel bidirectional cross-attention mechanism explicitly simulates the interaction between circuit constraints and environmental stress. Hardware verification indicates that the tracking efficiency of GNN-DSA on real PV panels is 99.1%–99.6%, on solar array simulators is 99.99%, and the response time is less than 100 ms. Comparative analysis shows that compared with the multilayer perceptron baseline, GNN-DSA reduces the mean squared error by 45.6%, and compared with the state-of-the-art Crossformer model, it reduces it by 22.3%.

title: Exploring the Flexibility of Twin-Basin Tidal Range Power Plants Through Optimal Control
abstract: In twin-basin tidal range schemes, a type of tidal barrage with two water reservoirs, the variations in sea water level throughout the day are used to generate electrical power, without direct CO2 emissions. This study focuses on optimising the operation of twin-basin tidal barrages using different objective functions, namely: energy maximising, income maximising and demand matching. The novelty of the study relies on using moment-based control to transcribe the infinite-dimensional twin-basin barrage optimal control problem into a finite-dimensional nonlinear program. To test the controller performance, a case study in the Severn Estuary, in the Southwest of the U.K., is presented, where the tidal resource is one of the highest in the world. It is found that, under tailored optimal scheduling, the twin-basin scheme can effectively shift generation periods to achieve greater income (between 1% and 3%, in the income maximising case) or to match peak demand hours (in the demand matching case), showing the increased flexibility of tidal range power plants compared to more traditional renewables. In the study cases presented, there is general agreement between energy maximising and demand matching optimal operation, since, for the particular time interval chosen, the phase of the tide was well aligned with demand, suggesting that tidal range plants are inherently demand-following. Furthermore, a control strategy is proposed for twin-basin barrages that results in continuous power output, reducing the hours of stand-by of the turbines, and highlighting the potential of twin-basin barrage for clean and dispatchable electricity generation.

title: Optimal Operation Strategy for AA-CAES in Joint Energy and Regulation Markets: Managing SoC Deviations From Regulation Response
abstract: As a representative technology of physical long-duration energy storage, advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) is capable of providing joint energy and secondary frequency regulation (SFR) services, playing an important role in power system regulation. However, the nonlinear characteristics of AA-CAES poses a challenge, as tracking regulation signals induces shifts in the operating point and air consumption of AA-CAES, complicating the process for state-of-charge (SoC) management. This paper proposes an optimal operation strategy for AA-CAES in joint energy and SFR markets. First, the SoC deviation induced by regulation response of AA-CAES is analyzed, and a dynamic operation model for AA-CAES to provide joint energy and SFR capacity services incorporating deviation impacts is developed. Subsequently, a self-scheduling strategy accounting for the uncertainty of regulation signals is proposed. This strategy employs stochastic dynamic programming to construct value functions in the day-ahead stage, and develops a chance-constrained stochastic programming model for rolling optimization in the intra-day stage. Numerical simulations based on real-world AA-CAES plant data validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The results indicate that considering the SoC deviations increases the net revenue by 3.0%, while the adoption of chance constraints leads to net revenue increase of 4.3%.

title: Space telescope will reopen view of far-infrared sky
abstract: NASA’s $1.2 billion PRIMA will explore galaxy evolution and planetary birth

title: Snowball refrigeration of Earth’s crust mimics glacial erosion
abstract: Glaciation cools the crust by setting its surface temperature to 0°C or well below. During the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, these conditions were in place long enough to cool the entire crustal column. Although crustal thermal history can be deciphered by thermochronology, these data are typically interpreted to record depth changes due to burial or erosion. Thermal models of the crust under Cryogenian boundary conditions predict that thermochronometers were substantially altered in the upper quarter to half of the crust. This Snowball Earth refrigeration, with little to no coeval erosion, may have imparted a cooling signal mimicking up to 3‒5 km of glacial erosion. Rock cooling previously attributed to massive Snowball erosion and linked to the Great Unconformity may instead reflect a great refrigeration of Earth’s crust, with implications for thermochronology across other climate events.

title: Project will track Amazon biodiversity in real time
abstract: Leaders of $100 million effort will use automated detection methods and computer models to monitor species’ trends

title: Anticipatory Utility Operations With Long-Duration Hydrogen Storage and Carbon Market Synergies
abstract: When leveraged within carbon market mechanisms, hydrogen energy storage systems (HESS) offer a viable option for supporting low-carbon operation in vertically integrated utilities. However, a key challenge is that short-term operational decisions are made without explicit visibility of their long-term consequences, which are reflected through cumulative hydrogen and carbon constraints that ensure system feasibility. To bridge this time-scale gap, this paper proposes a reinforcement learning–augmented primal–dual rolling-horizon optimization framework. A trained future-aware regularizer incorporates long-term information into short-term decision-making, while a primal–dual scheme enforces cumulative constraints on hydrogen and carbon markets with computational tractability. Numerical studies on the IEEE 6-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus test systems demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and scalability. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework keeps annual terminal residuals negligible while reducing peak emissions, improving economic performance, and enabling seasonal load shifting across different system scales.

title: Optimal Operation Trajectory Control of Variable Speed Pumped Storage for Power System Frequency Regulation
abstract: Variable speed pumped storage (VSPS) possesses significant potential for power system frequency regulation. This paper proposes a novel optimal trajectory control for VSPS to enhance power system frequency response (FR) by fully leveraging its regulation potential, while maintaining its rotor speed stability. First, the speed stability of VSPS during FR process in both turbine and pump modes is investigated. Following this, an analytical expression for the rotor speed is derived, specifically for the turbine mode, given its susceptibility to speed instability. This expression enables not only an efficient assessment of rotor overspeed risks but also a precise characterization of critical points along the operational trajectory. Then, the design principles of additional power control for VSPS are proposed to achieve a smooth switch of operation stages. Based on these principles and derived expressions, the optimal operation trajectory of VSPS is determined by system disturbances and the unit’s operating conditions. This adaptability of the proposed strategy optimizes power response and strengthens FR capability. Furthermore, an overspeed control is developed to ensure rotor speed stability. Finally, the IEEE 39-bus system is utilized to test the proposed strategy under various operating conditions, demonstrating its superior performance in improving power system FR.

title: A Multi-Mode Sub-Synchronous Damping Controller for Renewable-Thermal-Bundled Power Transmission by LCC-HVDC System
abstract: With the increase of renewable power generation, multiple poorly-damped or unstable sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) modes induced by various devices may coexist in the renewable-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system, including SG-based torsional SSOs and converter-based electromagnetic SSOs. Due to the complex dynamic interactions, it is still challenging to develop the consistent interpretation of the control interactive mechanism for different SSO modes, and to design a supplementary controller for multi-mode SSO suppression. To address these, this paper establishes the system equivalent single-input single-output (SISO) transfer function model for each SSO mode, by retaining its dominant energy storage element dynamic of the correlated device, and then their respective SSO stability is evaluated from a unified damping torque perspective. Subsequently, the interaction paths of key control loops contributing to the damping of each SSO mode are derived. On this basis, a damping enhancement capability index is proposed to identify the preferred control loop for the damping controller placement. Based on phase compensation and gain adjustment of the key control loop interaction path, a multi-mode sub-synchronous damping controller (MSDC) is proposed to realize the targeted damping compensation for different modes. Finally, the proposed MSDC approach is validated on a PV-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system, which effectively suppresses the PV-induced, LCC-induced or SG-induced SSOs.

title: Active Power Regulation of Wind Turbine Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning Guided Active Disturbance Rejection Control
abstract: Enhancing the active power regulation ability of wind turbine is a crucial approach to improving the flexibility of new power systems. This paper proposes a coordinated optimization strategy for reinforcement learning (RL) guided error-based active disturbance rejection controller (EADRC). Firstly, a well-established EADRC framework is employed, in which an extended state observer estimates and compensates for system disturbances in real time, thereby enhancing the system’s disturbance rejection capability and adaptability. Secondly, a Markovian decision process is integrated into the EADRC, allowing RL to adaptively tuning EADRC parameters in real time. This innovative integration of data-driven learning with disturbance rejection control enables the system to achieve optimal active power responses across diverse operating scenarios. Finally, simulations on a 5 MW wind turbine show that this proposed strategy outperforms conventional control methods in both active power tracking accuracy and system dynamic response, significantly enhancing the robustness of wind turbine control. This provides effective technical support for large-scale wind power integration in new power systems.

title: Multi-objective Non-causal Optimal Control of an Active Pumping System for a Floating Wind Platform
abstract: Semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) are susceptible to undesirable wave- and wind-induced pitch motion which may be reduced by control strategies. Presently these mainly rely on passive damping, which becomes ineffective under varying sea states. To address this issue, this paper proposes an active pumping strategy for water ballast using multi-objective noncausal optimal controller to suppress pitch motion by pumping water among three columns, thereby generating a counteracting moment against wave and wind excitations. Firstly, the dynamic model of the triple-column VolturnUS floating platform, coupled with hydrodynamic and aerodynamic forces, is developed using the Euler–Lagrange method. Based on this model, a multi-objective noncausal optimal controller is developed to balance pitch motion suppression and pumping power. When pitch minimization is prioritized, compared with the conventional passive damping control, the proposed method reduces the pitch motion by 85% but with high power demand. When power consumption is penalized, the controller can still reduce the pitch by 82% while lowering power usage by 95%, indicating a trade-off between motion suppression and pump energy consumption.

title: OLSchedLM: Leveraging Language Model for Economically-Driven and Curve-Aware Microgrid Online Scheduling Optimization
abstract: Online scheduling of microgrids is crucial for enhancing economic efficiency and stability. However, traditional model-based methods rely on accurate forecasts. Among data-driven approaches, reinforcement learning is constrained by training instability. Meanwhile, although imitation learning can learn policies directly from expert trajectories, conventional architectures suffer from limited sequence modeling capabilities and severe data hunger. To address these, this paper leverages the synergistic benefits of advanced architecture and inherent generalization capability of language models (LM). Specifically, we propose an online scheduling method based on LM named OLSchedLM, which adapts LM to this complex, continuous-control task. We frame the scheduling problem as a conditional sequence modeling task and train the LM-based agent on expert trajectories. These trajectories are generated by solving a bi-level programming model that incorporates domain knowledge and is designed to co-optimize electricity trading income and net load peak-valley difference. To pioneer a numerical-to-numerical paradigm, a suite of key adaptation techniques is introduced to bridge the domain gap between language and numerical control, including input and output projection layers and a two-stage parameter-efficient fine-tuning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OLSchedLM significantly outperforms established methods. Crucially, OLSchedLM’s excellent performance in few-shot experiments validates its effectiveness in addressing data hunger issue.

title: Negative-Sequence Impedance Provision of a Virtual Admittance-Based Inverter-Based Resource
abstract: While some grid-forming (GFM) inverter-based resources (IBRs) have both positive- and negative-sequence control units equipped to provide desired negative-sequence impedance, we find that a virtual admittance-based GFM-IBR with only positive-sequence unit can also provide desired negative-sequence impedance for grid code compliance. The goal of this paper is to provide an analysis to relate the negative-sequence impedance provision with the control scheme. To this end, an electromagnetic transient (EMT) testbed is developed to examine an IBR’s behavior subject to unbalanced grid faults. The negative-sequence voltage and current components are measured to calculate the equivalent negative-sequence impedance empirically. It is found that this impedance is indeed associated with the virtual impedance. The underlying mechanism is further discovered through complex vector-based analysis and frame conversion. The major takeaways are two-fold: (i) For a given control scheme, its negative-sequence impedance can be found analytically; (ii) inverter control can be designed more concisely to provide both positive- and negative-sequence impedances, in contract of having more complicated design with both positive- and negative-sequence control units included.

title: A Hybrid Interpretable Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robust Pitch Control of Large-Scale Wind Turbines
abstract: The increasing size and structural flexibility of offshore wind turbines (WTs) give rise to complex multi-modal dynamics and strong aeroelastic coupling, which render accurate control-oriented modelling impractical for large-scale turbines. While deep reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising model-free alternative for pitch control, its application to large WTs remains challenged by training stability, safety, and limited interpretability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a model-free, safety-oriented, and interpretable RL-based pitch control framework for large-scale WTs. A hybrid architecture is developed by embedding a gain-scheduled PI (GSPI) baseline within a residual RL structure, together with a smooth damping mechanism to ensure stable learning. In addition, a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based module is incorporated to interpret the learned policy through feature importance and time-resolved control patterns. Simulation results in OpenFAST using a 15 MW monopile WT demonstrate over 23% reductions in generator speed and power fluctuations under the nominal training scenario, together with mitigated tower and blade fatigue loads. Additional robustness evaluations under high-turbulence operating conditions further confirm that the proposed method maintains strong performance relative to the benchmark, and support safe, robust, and interpretable pitch control for large-scale WTs.

title: Lyapunov Compatibility-Based Adaptive Consensus Algorithm in PV-BESS Integrated Island DC Microgrids: A Dynamic State of Charge Balancing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel State-of-Charge (SoC)-based power allocation strategy for photovoltaic (PV)-based DC microgrids, leveraging an adaptive consensus algorithm to ensure SoC balance across Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) nodes. The primary control scheme employs inner-loop current droop control to mitigate disturbances arising from PV operation. The SoC-based power allocation strategy serves as a secondary control mechanism, designed to maintain a uniform SoC level across all BESS nodes via the adaptive consensus algorithm. This algorithm is compatible with a range of secondary control types, thereby mitigating battery degradation. Specifically, the stability and compatibility of the SoC-based power allocation strategy are rigorously proven by constructing a Lyapunov function. The proposed control strategy is simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK and in an OPAL-RT-based real-time simulation environment to demonstrate its effectiveness, in which the proposed adaptive consensus algorithm can accommodate two different secondary control strategies.

title: Are Mechanisms Important for AI to Identify Oscillation Sources? A Case Study
abstract: Grid-connected wind turbine generators (WTGs) may induce sub-synchronous oscillations (SSOs) in a power system. Due to the difficulty to gain the detailed parameters of the WTGs in practice, data-driven AI method is considered to be a potential solution to identify the trouble-making WTGs (or SSO sources) in the power system. Unlike the SSO mechanism observed in traditional power systems, numerous studies and real-world SSO events have indicated that the SSO mechanisms in wind power grid-connected systems can be more complex and varied. However, most AI-based works ignore the fact that the SSO can arise from different mechanisms. Typically, AI models are trained and evaluated using data generated from a single type of SSO mechanism. However, in practice, AI models may need to identify the sources of SSOs caused by different or even unknown mechanisms. This raises an interesting question: Are mechanisms important for AI to identify oscillation sources? This paper provides a preliminary exploration of this question through a specific case study that examines two general SSO mechanisms: negative resistance and open-loop modal resonance. Further explainability analysis is carried out to investigate whether the SSO mechanisms affect the performance of the AI models. Results of study cases and explainability analysis provide researchers and engineers with deeper insights into the generalization ability of AI with respect to SSO mechanisms.

title: Lightweight Series-Connected Topology and Control Strategy for Megawatt-Scale High-Altitude Wind Energy Systems
abstract: Scaling high-altitude wind energy systems (HAWESs) to the megawatt level faces a “weight–voltage” paradox: reducing tether mass requires medium voltage, yet conventional voltage-boosting components add prohibitive airborne mass. This paper resolves the paradox with a novel architecture using series-connected, diode-rectified generators, which inherently builds medium transmission voltage without onboard converters or transformers, enabling an ultralight airborne system controlled solely by a grid-side converter (GSC) located on the ground. A small-signal stability analysis considering generator parameter heterogeneity reveals that the system is robust to moderate wind variations, but becomes unstable when wind-speed heterogeneity drives a turbine into a region of positive torque–speed slope. The precise identification of this physical stability boundary provides the crucial design guidance needed to unlock a practical pathway toward the deployment of utility-scale HAWESs.

title: Stability Analysis of Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources Using Sequence Immittance Modeling and Dual Feedback Loop Criteria
abstract: Sequence immittance framework is an effective method to analyze the frequency-domain stability between the inverter-based resource (IBR) and the grid. However, there is a lack of a generic sequence immittance stability analysis framework for grid-forming inverter-based resource (GFM-IBR) considering frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling simultaneously. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a stability analysis framework for GFM-IBR using sequence immittance modeling and dual feedback loop criteria. Firstly, GFM-IBR is definitely modeled as impedance with self-stabilization based on two-port network by standardizing the immittance form for frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling. Secondly, the dual feedback loop criterion, integrating frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling, is proposed to avoid the need of checking the right-half-plane (RHP) poles. Finally, cases of grid-connected GFM-IBR verify the correctness of the proposed stability analysis framework. It is revealed that the voltage loop is the main reason for GFM self-stabilization, which enables GFM-IBR to be modeled in impedance form. Frequency coupling and AC-DC coupling greatly affect the stability of GFM-IBR as short circuit ratio (SCR) increases, which should not be neglected. The nonlinearity in synchronization and control of GFM-IBR affects frequency and AC-DC coupling more than that of grid-following inverter-based resource (GFL-IBR), while both exhibit dual uniformity.

title: Optimal Planning of Offshore Wind Farm Collector System Considering Intensive Sea Use
abstract: Driven by the global clean energy transition, the offshore wind power has been expanding rapidly worldwide. In offshore wind farms (OWFs), the electrical collector system (ECS) already accounts for a substantial portion of the total project cost, while emerging sea-use regulations call for compact, corridor-based cable layouts instead of traditional dispersed radial schemes. This paper proposes an OWF-ECS planning framework tailored to the intensive use of sea areas. We formulate a mixed-integer linear programming model (MILP) that incorporates the requirement of the intensive sea-use and uses the parallel-laying length of cables to represent spatial intensification. A clustering-based warm-start strategy and distance-based candidate-arc reduction are further designed to improve solution efficiency and scalability. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed framework can accommodate diverse sea-use requirements and intensification levels, consistently generating economically efficient and spatially intensive ECS layouts and obtaining high-quality feasible or optimal solutions within acceptable computation time.

title: Adaptive Perceptual Graph Learning for Robust Wind Power Forecasting Under Incomplete Observations
abstract: Reliable wind power forecasting plays a crucial role in enabling efficient scheduling and effective energy management in virtual power plants. However, incomplete data observations caused by sensor malfunctions and volatile environmental conditions significantly compromise the reliability of wind power forecasting. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust adaptive perceptual graph learning framework designed to enhance forecasting accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework uses an attention-gated GRU encoder to restore spatiotemporal dependencies under incomplete observations and integrates an adaptive graph convolution module to dynamically capture complex, non-stationary spatial correlations between wind turbines. To further promote physical consistency, a physics-informed discriminator is introduced as a plug-in component, guiding the model to align its outputs with the nonlinear aerodynamic relationship between wind speed and power generation. In addition, a sensitivity-aware adjustment strategy is developed to dynamically emphasize low-speed operating regimes. Comprehensive experiments conducted on real-world wind farm datasets show that the proposed method consistently surpasses baseline approaches, achieving a reduction of up to 35% in mean absolute percentage error, even under severe missing data scenarios.

title: Wind Speed Scenario Generation Under Typhoon Conditions via Prediction-Anchored Diffusion
abstract: Wind speed sequences under typhoon conditions exhibit complex spatio-temporal non-stationary characteristics, making it challenging for existing methods to control key features. This paper proposes a method for generating conditional wind speed scenarios based on a prediction-anchored diffusion model (PADM). First, a typhoon-aware time-series graph neural network (TA-TGNN) is developed, which constructs typhoon-aware adjacency matrices through trajectory similarity, temporal decay, and intensity similarity to characterize non-stationary dependencies. Second, a dual-dimensional adaptive attention mechanism (DDAM) is introduced, combining phase detectors and physical constraints to adaptively select and fuse key information across temporal and feature dimensions, thereby enhancing phase-aware prediction. Finally, PADM leverages deterministic prediction results as anchors and integrates hierarchical conditional encoding with temporal awareness to generate physically consistent and diverse wind speed scenarios. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method accurately reproduces the structural characteristics of typhoon wind speeds and captures variations under different conditions, while maintaining stability and consistency across various hyperparameter settings.

title: Multi-Source Coordinated Frequency Control of Grid-Connected Wind-Solar-Storage Power Station With Economic Improvement
abstract: Renewable power plant participating in frequency regulation often compromises power generation efficiency, and existing frequency regulation strategies generally neglect economic cost. To improve frequency security and economic efficiency, the paper proposes a multi-source coordinated frequency control (MCFC) for wind-solar-storage hybrid power stations. The MCFC control consists of two stages: frequency support and frequency recovery. During frequency support, photovoltaic (PV), wind, and energy storage are sequentially activated according to dynamic characteristics. The strategy allocates wind, PV, and energy storage outputs based on frequency security constraints to avoid excessive use of regulation energy and improve economic efficiency. During frequency recovery, wind turbine rotor speed is smoothly restored, and the recovery of the energy storage system (ESS) state of charge (SOC) is explicitly considered. Case studies are undertaken on the two-area power system with a wind-solar-storage hybrid power station and Guangshui hybrid collection station. The results show that MCFC can restore the frequency above safety thresholds and minimize renewable regulation energy to improve economic efficiency. Compared with existing methods, MCFC not only restores frequency to 49.5 Hz under a wider range of disturbances but also reduces economic index by up to 40% under mild disturbances.

title: HyMoOpt: A Hybrid Momentum Optimizer for Axial Induction Factor Control of Wind Farm Under Dynamic Wake Effects
abstract: This paper addresses the real-time axial induction factor (AIF) control problem for large-scale wind farms under dynamic wake effects and uncertain wind conditions. We first establish the mathematical formulation for the AIF control problem. The objective is to optimize collective power output while balancing the trade-off between energy revenue and the degradation of turbine lifespan caused by AIF adjustments. Building upon this foundation, we propose a novel hybrid momentum optimizer (HyMoOpt) controller. It combines a model-based gradient estimator for rapid convergence with a model-free feedback mechanism for robustness against model mismatch. A momentum term is further integrated to accelerate convergence and damp oscillations. We then derive an analytical bound on the gradient approximation error and prove that the proposed control algorithm achieves a sublinear convergence rate to the stationary point. Finally, the practical efficacy of HyMoOpt is demonstrated through simulations on a realistic 93-turbine offshore wind farm. Results show that it significantly enhances power output while maintaining strong adaptability under dynamic operational scenarios.

title: Coordinated Optimization of Coupled Power–Traffic Networks: A Hierarchical SUE Method Considering Behavioral Preferences and Uncertainty
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles intensifies the interdependence between transportation and power networks, posing operational challenges due to stochastic routing decisions and the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of charging demand. This paper proposes a hybrid decision-making framework that integrates user behavioral modeling with system-level optimization for coupled power-traffic networks. First, we develop network models that incorporate integrated energy stations (ESs) and heterogeneous vehicle classifications grouped by charging requirements and grid-response capabilities. Second, we formulate a hierarchical nested logit-based stochastic user equilibrium model to characterize multi-level user decisions under uncertainty. Furthermore, a collaborative power-traffic dispatch model is constructed to minimize generalized user costs, encompassing travel, charging, ES attributes, and power distribution network operation. A two-stage distributed solution algorithm is further developed to ensure computational tractability. Case studies on two test systems demonstrate the method's efficacy in characterizing user behavioral uncertainties and coordinating integrated power-traffic flows.

title: An LVRT Strategy for DFIG-BESS Based WECS With Maximum Voltage Support
abstract: The regional grid codes mandate that wind energy conversion systems (WECSs) stay connected during grid faults as long as terminal voltages stay above a specified level with respect to the fault duration. While existing low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategies for DFIG-WECSs satisfy these requirements, they do not guarantee maximum AC bus voltage recovery, which is essential for maintaining grid connectivity during severe faults. This paper presents an LVRT strategy for an on-grid DFIG supplying an AC microgrid. Rotor and stator overcurrent in the initial fault stage are limited using a crowbar. Then, a proposed coordinated RSC-GSC control aligns the DFIG-stator and transformer HV-side currents, maximizing the resultant AC bus injected current. Next, a modified adaptive voltage support scheme further maintains optimal real-time d-q axis current ratios for both converters (utilizing full capacity), so that overall injected current matches the network X/R ratio, ensuring maximum voltage recovery, regardless of the fault level, duration, location, wind speed, and wind farm condition. OPAL-RT real-time simulations confirm a 5.90% improvement in AC-bus voltage recovery and an 82% enhancement in post-fault transient response over recent literature.

title: Optimal Volt-VAR Curve Design for Inverter-Based Resources in Distribution Grids
abstract: The electric distribution grid has undergone rapid evolution, with customers increasingly adopting distributed energy resources (DERs). Conventional grid devices, like static reactive power compensators, were installed to address specific operational needs under traditional load conditions and are often not automated, making them less effective in today’s dynamic grid. Uncoordinated DER operation can further exacerbate issues, causing overvoltage, reverse reactive power flow, substation congestion, and low load power factor (LPF), highlighting the limitations of legacy grid assets. This paper presents an innovative methodology to design optimal volt-VAR curves (VVCs) for inverters to mitigate these challenges. To facilitate convergence and accelerate the computation of the optimal power flow (OPF) problem, a linear three-phase network power flow solver is employed to minimize reactive power flow through the substation and enhance the voltage profile within the distribution grid. Unlike existing approaches that use static VVCs or determine VVCs for each time instant, the proposed method generates an optimal VVC for each PV inverter over a specified period, while also producing location-specific curves. The approach is demonstrated on the IEEE 123-Node feeder and a large-scale real feeder with multiple PV inverters, showing improvements in substation LPF and feeder voltage profiles.

title: EMT-EMT Co-Simulation for Large-Scale Offshore Wind Integration in the New York State Grid
abstract: The rapid integration of large-scale offshore wind (OSW) farms and inverter-based resources (IBRs) presents unprecedented challenges for power system stability and protection. While electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation provides the necessary fidelity to capture fast control interactions, modeling an entire regional grid alongside detailed OSW models exceeds the computational capacity of single real-time simulators. This paper presents the practical design, implementation, and validation of a distributed real-time EMT–EMT co-simulation framework to evaluate the integration of 9 GW of offshore wind into the New York State (NYS) power grid. By interfacing heterogeneous real-time simulators of RTDS and OPAL-RT via an Aurora-based fiber-optic communication link and a Transmission Line Model (TLM), the computational burden is effectively distributed. A comprehensive experimental evaluation is conducted, including a direct comparison between analog and fiber-optic interconnections. The results demonstrate that the Aurora-based fiber interface significantly improves latency, synchronization accuracy, and transient waveform fidelity compared to traditional analog setups. Ultimately, this application study demonstrates how the proposed framework overcomes the limitations of traditional interfaces, enabling high-fidelity, real-time stability assessment of the NYS grid under severe fault conditions and providing actionable insights to de-risk large-scale OSW deployment.

title: An Enhanced Grid-Forming Control Strategy for DC-Coupled Alkaline Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Recent years have seen the research on the participation of Alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs) in power grid regulation gained significant traction. In particular, the participation of AWEs in grid-forming (GFM) services is precisely an urgent research topic at present. However, regarding the involvement of AWEs in GFM services, existing studies are typically limited to single AWE units or rely on communication for controlling multiple AWEs. Nor have they considered the capacity variation characteristics of AWEs. Furthermore, the unique topologies of DC-coupled AWE systems require special consideration. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced GFM control strategy for DC-coupled AWE systems. Specifically, the proposed control scheme includes two key improvements. First, a temperature-driven droop control is employed to enable coordinated operation among individual AWE units. Second, an improved DC-link voltage synchronized control (IDVSC) is proposed for the voltage source converter (VSC). Furthermore, the proposed strategy is fully decentralized, allowing both AWE units and the VSC to provide GFM services. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: A Distributed Two-Stage Framework for the Co-Scheduling of Power, Heat and Hydrogen Networks With Heterogeneous Frequency Supports
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed two-stage framework for the co-scheduling of power, heat and hydrogen networks with primary and enhanced frequency supports. To address the bilinear terms inherent in the Nadir frequency constraint, a distributed two-stage framework in the form of a fully-distributed computational pipeline is proposed. In the first stage, FedOnce, a distributed learning architecture with one-shot communication, is proposed to coordinate the energy sectors to efficiently predict the total frequency reserves. These predictions serve as warm starts to generate accurate linearizations of the bilinear Nadir terms, which are then embedded into the second-stage convex optimization of power, heat and hydrogen networks through the decentralized alternating-direction method of multipliers with pre-keyed encryption. The underlying distributed computational pipeline helps resolve the dilemma between computational efficiency and information privacy, through both parallel learning and advanced encryption. Case studies demonstrate its significant improvements in computational efficiency (by 2 orders of magnitude), approximation gaps (by 4.2%) and frequency response characteristics.

title: Distributed Adaptive Coordination of Flexibility Resources for Real-Time Power Balancing in Islanded DC Microgrids
abstract: Modern DC microgrids (DC-MGs) typically incorporate Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), energy storage systems, and local loads. In islanded DC-MGs, effective coordination of these components is essential for secure and reliable operation, given the intermittent nature of RESs and the uncertain demand profile. This paper employs electric spring topology to enhance flexibility through the smart management of both energy stored in batteries, and loads, in the case that the generation capacity of multiple RESs—operating with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm—is insufficient to meet demand. Besides, a distributed adaptive droop-based scheme is designed concerning a trade-off between common bus voltage regulation and proper current/power sharing among units. This distributed scheme benefits from a low-bandwidth communication interface among the in-service units to collect required data for adaptive estimation of droop gains. To ensure reliable operation of the DC-MG, batteries' capacity and State-of-Charge (SoC) information are also incorporated into the energy-sharing strategy, aiming to maintain SoC balance among storage units during replenishment. The feasibility of the proposed approach is evaluated through a Power-Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) platform.

title: A Double-Machine Small-Signal Equivalence Method for Power Systems With GFL and GFM Converters via Eigenfunction Matching
abstract: Renewable power systems (RPSs) with both grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) power electronic converters (PECs) have become prevalent. Complex dynamic interactions in RPSs pose analytical challenges on stability analysis. In such a context, this paper proposes an equivalent double-machine system (EDMS) and associated solution methods for analyzing small-signal stability issues of RPSs with both GFL and GFM PECs. Focusing on dominant modes, the original closed-loop system is first transformed into two Schur-complemented-form models that capture dominant modes introduced by GFL and GFM, respectively, then reduced via modal perturbation to equivalent single-machine subsystems (ESMSs), and finally, reconstructed into an EDMS that simultaneously captures the dominant modes introduced by both GFL and GFM PECs. The proposed method makes the most use of the equivalence of dominant eigenfunctions among the original system, the ESMSs, and the EDMS. Complementary solution approaches are developed for both white-box and black-box scenarios. The EDMS framework provides clear physical interpretability, i.e., a double-machine system, offering a scalable tool for dynamic analysis and stability evaluation in RPSs with GFL and GFM PECs. title: Frequency-Sharing Scheme for IPC-CSC Offshore Wind MTDC Systems Using Logistic Function
abstract: The current source converter-based multi-terminal DC (CSC-MTDC) system with improved phase control (IPC) method provides a promising solution for transmitting offshore wind power to multiple AC grids. However, the AC voltage control mechanism of such systems has not been fully investigated, and the inherent DC decoupling characteristics make it difficult to suppress frequency disturbances caused by wind speed fluctuations. To address these issues, this paper establishes the mathematical model of the IPC-CSC and proposes an offshore AC voltage control strategy by constructing intermediate variables, thereby ensuring the stable operation of the overall system. Furthermore, a frequency-sharing coordinated control strategy is proposed, where independent power and frequency control loops and voltage compensation are introduced. Thus, multiple receiving AC systems can jointly share power disturbances and fully utilize frequency regulation resources. In addition, an adaptive droop control method based on a logistic function is designed to provide smooth and bounded frequency support under different levels of frequency deviation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategies is validated through simulation and hardware-in-the-loop experiment results.

title: Wind Farm Cooperative Yaw Predictive Control Against Model Uncertainty via Continuous Learning From SCADA Data
abstract: Cooperative yaw control is a critical solution to reduce wake effect and improve power generation of wind farms, and its implementation based on analytical wake model is crucial to realizing its engineering practice. However, the inherent model uncertainty raises challenges. To this end, this paper proposes an application-oriented framework that allows SCADA data to engage cooperative yaw control, which can improve model adaptability and ensure power gain. First, considering the operation principle of industrial yaw system, a novel cooperative yaw predictive control with yaw rate as control action is introduced. Importantly, a continuous learning strategy against model uncertainty is proposed, which is composed of three mechanisms: outlier online detection using model prior knowledge, working scenario generation by distance dependent Chinese restaurant processes, and parameter learning with Bayesian inference. Finally, the result derived from Penmanshiel wind farm demonstrates that the proposed strategy can assimilate SCADA data well with a promising potential for engineering application of model-based cooperative yaw control.

title: Dual-Port DC Wind Turbines Based Offshore Wind Power Integration System Embedded With Power Balance and Fault Ride-Through Capability
abstract: In offshore wind farm (OWF) integration systems, emerging DC collection and transmission schemes (all-DC) necessitate the series-parallel connection of DC wind turbines (WTs) to boost the DC collection voltage. However, power imbalance among DC WTs impairs the overall efficiency of the integration system. To address the inherent limitations of the all-DC approach, this paper proposes a dual-port DC wind turbine-based DC collection and transmission topology for OWF integration. Where the DC ports of each DC WT are connected in series to elevate the DC collection voltage, while the AC ports of adjacent DC WTs are connected to decouple the power of DC WTs. Firstly, the topology, operating principle and control strategy of the all-DC integration system incorporating the proposed DC WT are introduced, and the power balance mechanism is analyzed. Then, a comprehensive fault ride-through (FRT) method is proposed to handle various fault types. Furthermore, the parameter design method and overall evaluation of the proposed integration system are conducted. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed all-DC integration system under different operation scenarios is validated in PSCAD/EMTDC.

title: Supervisory Control Framework for a Hybrid PV-BESS Inverter Under Power Export Constraint
abstract: This paper presents a practical supervisory energy management framework for a hybrid photovoltaic (PV)-battery energy storage system (BESS) inverter operating under a grid export constraint. The strategy reconciles two conflicting objectives: to maximize PV energy utilization and to minimize BESS cycling energy while requiring almost no inverter firmware modification. Unlike conventional inverter-embedded methods with limited control flexibility, the proposed framework introduces a vendor-independent supervisory controller that interfaces with a hybrid inverter through standard Modbus/RS-485 communication. A compact five-mode control architecture enables rapid adaptation to load variations, improved PV operating point selection, and coordinated BESS dispatch with minimal cycling stress. Experimental validation across eight representative scenarios spanning seasonal irradiance variability and weekday/weekend load patterns demonstrates significant performance gains. During summer, spring, and autumn, grid import decreases by 93%, the self-sufficiency ratio increases from 45.7–65.5% to 74.6–78.9%, and PV curtailment decreases consistently. Furthermore, the annual grid expenditure is reduced by nearly 80%. Economic analysis indicates favorable viability, with a payback period of 1.9 years when accounting for grid savings and conservative BESS lifetime extension benefits. The proposed supervisory energy management system achieves superior PV utilization, enhanced operational autonomy, and substantial economic benefits, offering a scalable, retrofit-compatible solution for export-constrained residential and commercial PV-BESS installations.

title: Low-Frequency Oscillation Stability Evaluation of Grid-Forming-Converter-Dominated Power Systems
abstract: To address the well-known concern of sub/super-synchronous oscillation issues driven by the interaction among grid-following converters, there is an increasing use of grid-forming (GFM) converters for renewable integration into power grids. However, it has recently been reported that low-frequency oscillation issues occur in a multi-converter system dominated by GFM converters (named as MCS-GFMC). Since the low-frequency oscillation instability mechanism remains unclear, it is challenging to identify this type of oscillation issues in realistic MCS-GFMCs. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a method for quickly identifying the low-frequency oscillation stability issues from the perspective of grid strength. We first analyze the theoretical relationship between grid strength and low-frequency oscillation stability in a single-GFM-converter system by the system’s closed-loop characteristic equation. Then, this analytical relationship is extended to MCS-GFMCs for developing the proposed method. This method is applicable to large-scale MCS-GFMCs, even with “black-boxed” converters. Two test systems are provided to validate the proposed method.

title: Robust Coordinated Prescriptive Power System Dispatch: Bridging Adjustable Robust OPF and Multiple Probabilistic Predictions
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable generation introduces substantial uncertainty into short-term power system operations, challenging cost-effective dispatch under network constraints. In conventional predict–then–optimize frameworks, uncertainty bounds are learned independently and treated as fixed inputs to robust optimal power flow (OPF), limiting feedback from operational decisions to improve uncertainty representation. This paper proposes a robust semi-end-to-end coordinated decision framework that bridges probabilistic forecasting and robust optimization for prescriptive power system dispatch. Probabilistic prediction models estimate one-step-ahead renewable generation and load intervals, which are incorporated into a robust OPF model through the induced uncertainty sets. The proposed framework integrates three components: a machine learning layer, a robust decision-making layer, and a decision evaluation layer. During the forward pass, predicted uncertainty bounds are converted into robust dispatch decisions, while in the backward pass, gradients are propagated through the optimization layer to train forecasting models using task-level operational feedback. Numerical results demonstrate stable training and consistent economic improvements over the conventional predict–then–optimize approach, achieving average total-cost reductions of 14.3% and 16.0% on the IEEE 5- and 30-bus systems, respectively. The improvement on the IEEE 118-bus system is smaller because uncertainty-related costs account for a limited portion of total operating costs. Under the adopted single-interval DC-based dispatch formulation, the proposed method also learns tighter uncertainty intervals (around 25% narrower) while reducing reserve-related slack activation under stressed operating conditions.

title: An Optimal Offering and Operating Strategy for Wind-Storage Operators Participating in Grid Inertial Response and Frequency Regulation
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy generation weakens the power system’s inertia support capability, thereby exacerbating the risk of frequency instability. This paper proposes a bi-level optimal offering and operating strategy that enables wind-storage operators to provide inertial response and frequency regulation service in the power grid with high renewable penetration. The upper level takes operational costs as the objective to quantify the time-varying ability of wind-storage operators for virtual inertia and frequency responses, and the energy dispatch and frequency-regulation services of wind-storage operators are optimally coordinated to support power grid operations at the lower level. Then, the differences in inertial response and frequency regulation dynamics between synchronous generators and wind-storage systems are quantitatively characterized by incorporating frequency-response delays. The frequency security constraints that account for the dynamic inertia characteristics of wind-storage systems are established. Finally, the original bi-level optimization problem is reformulated into an equivalent single-level problem using duality theory and KKT conditions, so as to derive an effective cost-reflective mechanism for providing inertia and frequency regulation services. Comparative results demonstrate that the participation of wind-storage systems in frequency regulation markets can significantly enhance the economic efficiency of power system operations.

title: Hybrid Fault Isolation and Power Control of Wind Turbine Generators Based on Stacked UIO
abstract: The stable operation of megawatt-class wind turbines directly impacts grid connection performance. As complex electromechanicald systems operating in variable environments, time-varying hybrid faults frequently occur, posing challenges for fault-tolerant control (FTC). This paper proposes novel approaches for hybrid fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant controller design. First, a collaborative architecture for a stacked unknown input observer (UIO) is constructed for integrated fault diagnosis of hybrid faults in wind turbine generators (WTGs). The designed stacked UIO strategy can decouple and separately estimate the dynamic of speed and torque, achieving effective time-varying hybrid fault diagnosis. Second, given the disturbances, uncertainties, and discrete-time nature of WTGs, the asymptotic stability of the proposed UIO is established using Lyapunov’s theorem. Finally, combining fault information, a two-degree-of-freedom model predictive control strategy is adopted to achieve FTC while also considering power stability tracking. Simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate time-varying faults in WTG actuators and sensors, and maintain reliable control performance under hybrid fault conditions, thereby verifying its effectiveness as a comprehensive FTC solution.

title: Rotor-Angle Stability Enhancement Control for MMC-MTDC Systems Without Sending-End Power Reserves
abstract: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems are increasingly integrated into AC grids, making rotor-angle stability more critical. Improper HVDC dynamics during disturbances may weaken synchronizing torque and damping, thereby aggravating oscillations. This paper investigates the offshore wind farm (OWF)-based multi-terminal DC (MTDC) system and analyzes the impact of its power injections on grid rotor-angle stability. On this basis, a frequency-based power control logic is first proposed to enhance rotor-angle stability. Building on this logic, Lyapunov-based control laws are derived to coordinate active and reactive power both among multiple terminals (inter-terminal level) and within each converter under capacity constraints (intra-terminal level). To further optimize the coordinated control, an optimization framework is then designed, ensuring effective and secure support. Finally, considering the absence of power reserves at the sending-end OWF, a capacitor energy-based control strategy is proposed for MTDC systems to utilize all MMCs’ capacitor energy at the same time for stability support (device level), thereby expanding the available support energy and further improving rotor-angle stability. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control are validated on the IEEE 39-bus system via PSCAD/EMTDC and MATLAB co-simulation.

title: Bilevel Optimization for Green Hydrogen-to-Ammonia Synthesis System Considering Complex Dynamic Processes and Uncertainties
abstract: The wind-powered green hydrogen-to-ammonia system offers a promising pathway for utilizing marine renewable energy; however, its economic viability is constrained by the strongly nonlinear dynamics of ammonia synthesis and the inherent stochasticity of wind power generation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a bilevel scheduling framework. In the upper layer, a reduced-order Trend- and Structure-constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (TS-PINN) model is developed by embedding trend priors and mechanistic constraints, effectively capturing the nonlinear characteristics of the ammonia synthesis process with significantly reduced computational effort. An improved Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm is then employed to co-optimize operational strategies and key reactor setpoints, including bed temperature and pressure. In the lower layer, a Wasserstein-distance-based distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model is established to coordinate hydrogen production and storage operations to hedge against wind power uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an effective balance among modeling accuracy, economic performance, and operational robustness, while accounting for coupled reaction–heat-transfer dynamics and renewable generation uncertainty.

title: ShadowSense: Edge Optimized Self-Supervised Learning for Dynamic Shadow Mapping of Solar Panels
abstract: We introduce ShadowSense, a self-supervised, edge-deployable framework for dynamic shadow mapping and short-term PV power forecasting. Unlike prior methods that require labor-intensive manual annotations or rely on overly complex physical models, ShadowSense uses transient power dips as weak supervision signals, enabling fully unsupervised learning from synchronized sky imagery and power measurements. The architecture integrates a masked spatiotemporal autoencoder to learn cloud motion dynamics, a differentiable geometric projection module to adapt to diverse panel orientations, and a causal alignment system to maintain temporal correspondence between cloud shadows and power responses. Evaluated over 122,400 observations across 92 days in Kaunas, Lithuania, the system achieved a 32.7% reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) compared to baselines, captured 92.3% of rapid power ramps, and operated with an average inference latency of 66 ms and energy cost of 0.52 J per prediction on a solar-powered NVIDIA Jetson Nano, demonstrating scalable, real-time PV forecasting in resource-constrained environments.

title: Low-Temperature Activation and High Capacity Hydrogen Storage in TiVCr-BCC Alloys Modified with AB5 Intermetallics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Effective hydrogen storage remains a significant barrier in the deployment of metal hydrides for energy applications, primarily due to kinetic limitations and high pretreatment requirements in high-capacity body-centered cubic (BCC) alloys. This study systematically investigates the influence of incremental additions of AB5-type intermetallic La0.9Ce0.1Ni5, (0–15 wt %) on the hydrogen sorption properties of Ti0.48V0.26Cr0.26 BCC solid solution alloys. The results proved that modest additions of La0.9Ce0.1Ni5 significantly reduce the activation temperature from >350 to 80 °C, enabling fast hydrogen absorption kinetics (t90% reduced to as low as 70 s) while maintaining high hydrogen capacities up to 3.5 wt %. The synergistic interaction between the BCC matrix and AB5 secondary phases, enriched in catalytically active Ni sites, promotes efficient hydrogen dissociation and diffusion pathways. Thermodynamic analysis reveals increased plateau pressures and improved reversible desorption. These results demonstrate that AB5-type intermetallics provide a viable route for overcoming the activation barrier in BCC-based alloys, enabling high-capacity and low-temperature hydrogen storage systems.

title: Photosensitive PbTe Dielectric Films as Universal Functional Modules for Optically Tunable Terahertz Metamaterials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Optically tunable dynamic terahertz (THz) metamaterials hold significant application prospects in real-time THz modulation, high-speed communications, intelligent sensing, and nondestructive testing. However, existing optically modulated THz metamaterials commonly face critical bottlenecks such as limited photosensitive material systems, complex fabrication processes, stringent high-intensity excitation conditions, and poor universality of device architectures. To address these issues, we propose the narrow-bandgap PbTe semiconductor as a photosensitive dielectric layer for constructing optically tunable THz metamaterials. The PbTe thin film was fabricated via facile and cost-effctive electron beam evaporation and incorporated as dielectric layers, with quartz substrates underneath and metallic resonator arrays of various materials and geometries constructed on top, thereby forming complete THz metamaterial architectures. Experimental results show that owing to the narrow bandgap of PbTe at approximately 1.12 eV, significant THz modulation can be achieved with extremely low optical excitation density of 12.2 mW/cm2, which is far below the natural solar intensity. Combined photocurrent spectroscopy, Mott Schottky analysis, and Drude–Smith model fitting elucidate that the increase in photoinduced carrier concentration and the decrease in relaxation time jointly induce an increase in the real part and a decrease in the imaginary part of the complex permittivity of PbTe, which constitute the microscopic physical mechanism underlying the optically induced impedance mismatch and enhanced phase delay. More importantly, regardless of the material composition (Au/Cu) or geometry (square-shape/cross-shape) of the metallic resonators, the same optical modulation trend remains robust, consistently exhibiting enhanced impedance mismatch, increased reflectivity, reduced absorptance, and improved phase-delay capability. Furthermore, increasing the thickness of the PbTe dielectric layer can also further enhances the modulation depth of these effects, fully demonstrating its excellent universality and design flexibility. This work presents an innovative strategy of employing PbTe semiconductors to construct optically tunable terahertz metamaterials, which can serve as an optical functional module that imparts dynamic tunability to arbitrary THz metamaterials, featuring excellent universality, low energy consumption, and high modulation depth, holding significant potential for applications in photoresponsive terahertz devices.

title: Ultrahigh Ductility in the BCC Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 Refractory Multiprincipal Element Alloy: Energetic and Electronic Origins
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Recent experimental discovery of the ultrahigh ductility of the body-centered cubic (BCC) Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 refractory multiprincipal element alloy (RMPEA) exhibits a clear distinction from the MoNbTaW RMPEA with low ductility. To unravel the physical origins of this remarkable ductility, this study employs first-principles calculations to investigate the factors governing intrinsic ductility of the RMPEAs. The energy calculation results indicate a stronger tendency for double cross-slip, dislocation multiplication, and twinning deformation of the Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 RMPEA. Integrated with fracture criteria, it is further confirmed that multiple dislocations and twins can emit from the crack tip in this alloy. Analysis of the electron structure reveals that the compositional substitution induces the charge delocalization, bonding metallization and a higher and smoother density of states curve near the Fermi level of the Nb45Ta25Ti15Hf15 RMPEA. Furthermore, increasing Nb content generally raises the calculated fault and surface energies, while favorable plasticity tendencies persist across the investigated BCC configurations. Nb addition can increase the energetic barrier to fault formation and dislocation nucleation without suppressing the intrinsic propensity for crack-tip plasticity over a broad composition range. These findings can provide energetic and electronic insights into the intrinsic ductility of the BCC RMPEAs containing group IV elements.

title: Bioinspired Continuous 2.5D Woven Miura-ori Metasurface for Mechanically Tunable Microwave Filtering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rigid mechanically reconfigurable frequency-selective surfaces (FSSs) provide well-defined geometric tuning but are difficult to conform to complex curved surfaces, whereas conventional frequency-selective fabrics (FSFs) are conformable. Reported origami FSFs, however, generally use uniform textile substrates with fold lines introduced after textile fabrication, limiting direct structural guidance of Miura-ori reconfiguration. Here, we develop a bioinspired continuous 2.5D woven Miura-ori frequency-selective metasurface. Multilayer angle-interlock facet regions and single-layer plain-weave hinge regions are continuously integrated within a single aramid substrate through electronic Jacquard weaving. The facet regions support printed cross-shaped conductive units, whereas the hinge regions directly form the Miura-ori fold lines and guide the woven metasurface along the designed folding paths. These region-specific functions guide the woven metasurface along a defined Miura-ori deformation pathway, enabling monotonic folding-dependent frequency tuning over the investigated folding states. Under normal incidence, the measured resonant frequency decreases monotonically from 9.02 to 8.05 GHz as the folding angle decreases from 90° to 45°, yielding a tuning span of 0.97 GHz. At a folding angle of 60°, the resonant-frequency variation is 0.57 GHz over incidence angles from 0° to 45°, while the maximum variation among the investigated conformal configurations is 0.21 GHz. Full-wave simulations and a transmission-line equivalent circuit model with effective circuit parameters fitted using particle swarm optimization were used to interpret the folding-induced redshift. The redshift is associated with reduced projected separation between cross-shaped conductive units on adjacent facets, enhanced near-field coupling, increases in the fitted equivalent inductance and total equivalent capacitance, and additional phase accumulation represented by the calculated effective propagation-length coefficient. These results provide a textile-based strategy for mechanically tunable microwave filtering on curved surfaces.

title: Fe-Doped Non-stoichiometric Na3.4Co2.4(PO4)1.4P2O7 Cathode for High-Energy-Density Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Na4Co3(PO4)2P2O7 is a representative mixed polyanionic cathode with a high operating voltage and high energy density. However, insufficient cycling stability is the core bottleneck constraining the widespread application of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy that combines non-stoichiometry with Fe2+ doping to construct Na3.4Co2.4–xFex(PO4)1.4P2O7 (NCFPP-x), which not only enhances phase purity but also improves material stability. Through ex situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy-distribution of relaxation times and galvanostatic intermittent titration technique analyses, it is demonstrated that Fe doping leads to the reduced charge transfer impedance and enhanced Na+ diffusion coefficient. The in situ XRD characterization results demonstrate a highly reversible incomplete solid-solution reaction mechanism during the Na+ intercalation and deintercalation processes. The NCFPP-1.2||Hard carbon (HC) full cell assembled with an HC anode delivers an energy density of 325 Wh kg–1, retaining 80.0% after 200 cycles. The present work offers important theoretical basis and experimental support for the advancement of high-voltage polyanion-type cathode materials.

title: Programmable Artificial Hydrolase Based on Minimalistic Cross-α/Cross-β Amyloid Assemblies
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Enzymes, which catalyze nearly all biochemical processes, are delicately organized special substances composed of large proteins, specific secondary structures, distinct amino acid residues with precise positioning, and often metal cofactors. Reconstruction of enzymatic catalytic domains within fully artificial systems has become an interesting but challenging subject, largely due to limited understanding of their evolutionary processes. A long-standing opportunity in the generation of artificial or miniature enzymes has been to design building units capable of performing similar chemistry without the structural complexity of full proteins. Herein, by using a reductionist approach, we explore the sequence–structure–activity landscapes of enzyme evolution by investigating minimal amyloid-forming analogous peptides. Our results reveal that amyloid peptides without encoding canonical catalytic amino acids (like Lys, Ser, His, Glu/Asp) or metal cofactors can nevertheless catalyze ester hydrolysis through fibril-dependent substrate binding. Minor sequence variations alter supramolecular organization and reorganize solvent-exposed terminal groups, creating distinct catalytic microenvironments and activities. Combining experiments with molecular simulations, we show that these fibril surfaces present topologically different binding grooves that modulate the association of the model substrate. This sequence–structure–activity paradigm of de novo biocatalysts holds promise for predictable and robust construction of peptide-based new functional materials applicable in chemical and biochemical synthesis.

title: Prediction-Based Interval Voltage Regulation Involving PV-BESS Coordination
abstract: Modern distribution networks face critical voltage security challenges due to high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESSs). Traditional regulation strategies have proven inadequate in mitigating rapid voltage violations caused by power fluctuations. Therefore, a prediction-based proportional coordinated power compensation method is proposed for interval voltage regulation (VR). Firstly, an improved convolutional neural network model is established to predict variable power flows by considering PV and load characteristics, enabling accurate voltage profile prediction. Then, the crucial bus with the most voltage violation is identified, and the optimal coordination ratios for reactive power compensation (RPC) and active power compensation (APC) are determined by an optimization process based on dynamic sensitivity analysis. Furthermore, the crucial bus VR method sequentially allocates RPC from PV inverters and APC from BESSs using a sensitivity-based proportional coordination. Finally, the test results demonstrate an effective VR across all buses over a 24-hour operation, with total RPC and APC requirements reduced by 41.8% and 34.5% in a real 10-bus network, and by 79.1% and 39.5% in the IEEE 123-bus network, respectively.

title: Large-Area Polyaniline/Carbon Nanotube Composite Film for the Zn-Ion Electrochromic Window toward Energy-Sustainable Buildings
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polyaniline (PANI) holds promise as cathode material for energy-saving electrochromic windows due to its reversible optical modulation and intrinsic energy storage capability. However, the simultaneous realization of large-area electrode fabrication, high electrochromic performance, and superior energy storage remains a key challenge for PANI-based electrochromic windows. Herein, we report a scalable and facile approach to fabricate a PANI/carbon nanotube (CNT)/PANI composite film on transparent conductive glass through combination of chemical oxidation polymerization and spray coating. The introduction of a CNT interlayer, low-temperature polymerization of PANI, and dual-cathode design collectively endows the hybrid structure with enhanced electrical conductivity, accelerated ion diffusion, and increased active sites. The resulting Zn-ion electrochromic device delivers a high optical modulation of 82.3% at 650 nm, a low coloration transmittance of 5.4%, fast switching speeds (coloration/bleaching time: 5.8 s/4.6 s), and a neutral tint in the colored state. Notably, the device also exhibits attractive energy storage performance with a specific capacitance of 45.6 mF cm–2 and an energy density of 12.4 μWh cm–2. Under simulated solar irradiation, the electrochromic window achieves an optical power modulation of 67.3% and enables a temperature regulation of 6.6 °C by switching between transparent and colored states. As a proof of concept, a large-area prototype (10 × 10 cm2) demonstrating uniform color change and good adhesive stability is presented. This work provides a scalable and effective route toward high-performance, conducting polymer-based electrochromic windows for intelligent thermal management and on-site energy recovery, contributing to sustainable energy utilization and building energy efficiency.

title: Breaking the Drivability-Threshold-Voltage Trade-off in 40 nm Vertical Gate-All-Around Oxide FETs via Spacer-Defined Offset Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spacer-defined offset engineering is presented as a structural strategy to enhance the on-state current (ION) of vertical gate-all-around (VGAA) amorphous indium–gallium oxide (IGO) field-effect transistors (FETs) while preserving threshold-voltage (VTH) control. Increasing the indium fraction in the IGO channel improved ION but simultaneously caused a pronounced negative VTH shift, revealing an observed trade-off in composition-based channel engineering. To circumvent this limitation, the SiO2 spacer thickness was scaled from 100 to 30 nm while maintaining the optimized IGO 6:3 channel composition. For IGO FETs with a gate length of 40 nm, the average ION increased from 1.24 ± 0.54 to 9.5 ± 1.94 μA as the spacer thickness was reduced from 100 to 30 nm, without inducing a negative VTH shift. For twenty 30-nm-spacer devices, the average VTH and subthreshold swing were 0.29 ± 0.05 V and 71.4 ± 4 mV/dec, respectively, with an apparent drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) factor of 3.7 mV/V. Y-function analysis, temperature-dependent measurements, and Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations revealed that the performance enhancement originated from reduced access resistance and electrostatic modulation of the source-side access region, while no statistically distinct spacer-dependent change in the effective source-side injection barrier was resolved. The optimized device also exhibited VTH shifts of only +79 and –26 mV under positive and negative bias-temperature stress, respectively, at 95 °C for 3600 s under effective gate fields of ±3 MV/cm, while the VGAA-based two-transistor zero-capacitor dynamic random-access memory (2T0C DRAM) cell exhibited a retention time exceeding 100 s. These results establish spacer-defined offset engineering as an effective structural design approach for oxide-semiconductor memory transistors that require both high ION and stable VTH operation.

title: Regulating Hydrothermal Deposition Kinetics via an Acid–Base Buffering Strategy for Efficient HTL-Free Sb2Se3 Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The hydrothermal method, known for its operational simplicity, environmental benignity, and low cost, has been established as a viable route for fabricating high-efficiency antimony selenide (Sb2Se3) photovoltaic devices. However, the closed nature of this system poses a significant challenge to gaining an intuitive and comprehensive understanding of the underlying reaction mechanisms during hydrothermal deposition. In this work, we reveal a “self-accelerating” phenomenon that occurs during the selenium releasing process from the sodium selenosulfate (Na2SeSO3) selenium precursor. To address this issue, this work introduced an HAc/Na2SO3 buffering pair to regulate the hydrothermal chemistry, thereby achieving controlled release of HSe- species. The introduction of the buffer additive promotes the heterogeneous nucleation of Sb2Se3 on the substrate and prolongs the sustained release of the Se source, enabling a thicker film with distinctly strengthened enhanced (221) and (301) crystallographic orientations. The resulting Sb2Se3 solar cell without a hole transport layer delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 6.77%. Overall, this work expands the possibilities for manipulating reaction pathways in solution-based deposition from a chemical perspective.

title: Single-Atom Modulation of Local Energy States in sp2-COF for TENG-based Corrosion Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In recent years, with the introduction of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to the field of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), effective charge separation, higher charge density, and faster charge transport rates have become the key challenges for improving the output performance of triboelectric power generation. Therefore, a series of fully conjugated covalent organic framework platforms connected through vinyl bonds were designed and synthesized in this study. The charge density and local energy levels were manipulated in a programmable way by changing a single atom in a local region of one of the monomers, and the correlation among the charge density, local energy states, and the performance of triboelectric power generation was discussed in detail. The results indicated that COF-2N@TENG demonstrated the best triboelectric power production capability, with a maximum current of 61.7 μA and a peak instantaneous power density of 2385.72 mW m–2. In the applications of self-powered corrosion protection, COF-2N@TENG showed remarkable cathodic protection capabilities. In addition, a series of theoretical calculations and experimental studies have shown the methods by which individual nitrogen atom locations control the orbital energy, surface potential, and local electron distribution. This study elevates the optimization of TENG performance from the traditional trial-and-error approach to the level of atomically precise molecular design. By chemically modifying COF materials through the localized modification of individual atoms while maintaining physical parameters such as morphology and pore size, it revealed the independent effects of enhanced electron affinity within the COF framework and surface charge density on TENG output performance. This provides a highly insightful atomic-level gene bank design paradigm for the development of customized, high-performance COF-based TENG materials.

title: Extracellular Electron Transfer from Photosynthetic Microalgae Modulates the Response of Electrolyte-Gated Organic Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
