The results indicate that particle motion under impulse voltage is probabilistic: 500 μm particles primarily exhibit in-place torsion and horizontal rolling, while 50 μm particles predominantly undergo diffusion and adhesion. Particles of both sizes exhibit four discharge morphologies, namely isolated luminous spots, semi-bridging discharge, two-segment discharge, and surface flashover. At higher voltages, 500 μm particles tend to form two-segment discharges, whereas 50 μm particles are more likely to produce isolated luminous-spot discharges, implying distinct pre-flashover pathways in which dispersed dust promotes distributed multi-spot bridging while coarse particles favor localized streamer initiation via stronger electron supply. The impulse voltage facilitates initial streamer inception and enhances the photoionization process. The resulting burst of force increases the likelihood of particles overcoming resistance and accelerating disintegration, which at that stage suppresses further discharge development. This study provides theoretical support for elucidating the potential hazards posed by metal particles within the mechanism housing of clean-air GIS.

title: Autonomous Optimal Control for Wind Farm Integrated MMC-HVDC System Under Sending-End Single-Phase to Ground Fault
abstract: The integration of large-scale wind farm (WF) with modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems is promising. However, this integration is challenged by the single-phase-to-ground (SLG) fault at sending-end overhead transmission lines. Existing SLG fault ride-through (FRT) strategies mainly focus on the fault stresses suppression and transient stability improvement. Less attention is paid to the grid voltage unbalance issue and the limited power transfer capability during SLG FRT. To address these issues, this paper proposes an autonomous optimal control (AOC) to enhance the SLG FRT performance. Firstly, considering the long-distance communication delays, autonomous optimization models are respectively established for MMC and WF, where MMC targets to maximize the power transmission while the WF aims to minimize the grid voltage unbalance. Secondly, with semi-definite relaxation (SDR) and second-order cone relaxation (SOCR), the original nonlinear nonconvex optimization models are transformed into computationally tractable convex formulations. Finally, the autonomous optimization models of MMC and WF are independently solved merely based on local measurements, the solutions of which are taken as the control reference during SLG FRT. Compared with the existing SLG FRT control, the proposed AOC can guarantee the maximum transmission of active power for MMC and minimum grid voltage unbalance for WF. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed AOC.

title: Prediction Method for Audible Noise of High-Altitude Extra-High Voltage AC Transmission Lines Based on Long-Term Observations
abstract: Audible noise (AN) is a critical parameter in the economic and environmental design of extra-high voltage (EHV) AC transmission lines, especially in high-altitude regions. Although several altitude correction factors and AN prediction methods have been proposed based on corona cage tests and long-term observations, the accuracy remains uncertain owing to the limited measurement data from high-altitude transmission lines. This study addresses this gap through long-term observations of four EHV transmission lines on the Tibetan Plateau, combined with existing corona cage test results. The cumulative distribution of AN in rainy weather was obtained from various observation stations. By comparing measured values from stations at different altitudes and combining the experimental results from a movable corona cage, an altitude correction method for AN was developed. Subsequently, by comparing statistical data from four high-altitude observation stations with predicted results from different approaches, the predicted values were found to be overestimated. An improved prediction method for AN in rainy weather was proposed. Additionally, based on the statistical differences observed over one year at multiple long-term observation stations, a method for evaluating AN under varying weather conditions was investigated. A predictive model for AN under different rainfall conditions was developed based on correlation and multiple regression analyses, and its accuracy was validated. The findings of this study provide a crucial reference for the prediction and evaluation of AN from EHV AC transmission lines in high-altitude regions.

title: Robust Protection Coordination of Directional Over-Current Relays in AC Microgrids
abstract: Conventional protection coordination in AC microgrids often assumes a single network topology to determine optimal settings for Directional Over-Current Relays (DOCRs), leading to miscoordinations when unconsidered scenarios arise. Unlike previous schemes considering various network scenarios, this paper introduces a novel two-stage protection coordination scheme for DOCRs in an AC microgrid using a robust optimization approach to address the above limitation, wherein the first stage determines two optimal DOCRs settings, one each for Grid-Connected Mode (GCM) and Islanded Mode (IM), and the associated dual variables. The second stage identifies the worst-case scenarios for each DOCR pair, including line and Distributed Generator (DG) outages, varying DGs' injections, and resistive faults, each in GCM and IM. The proposed approach significantly reduces the protection coordination constraints required to obtain the settings, thereby reducing solver execution time and improving computational efficiency. Extensive tests on modified IEEE <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$13-$</tex-math></inline-formula>bus and IEEE <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$34-$</tex-math></inline-formula>bus AC microgrids with synchronous and inverter-interfaced DGs, and comparison with previous schemes underscore the reliability of the proposed approach under diverse AC microgrid operating conditions.

title: Critical End-Effect at Sea-to-Land Transition of Three Core Submarine Cables
abstract: At the sea-to-land transition or offshore interfaces, three-core submarine cables are separated into individual single-core cables arranged in a flat configuration. This separation, combined with protective layers over metallic sheaths that impart semiconductive properties and cause spatial bonding, results in localized increases in circulating sheath currents in the submarine portion of the installation. Despite potential thermal consequences in offshore cable projects, this specific issue has received limited attention in the existing literature; consequently, this paper presents a novel examination of this end-effect phenomenon. An analytical model is developed in the paper and cross-validated with a comprehensive three-dimensional Finite Element Method (FEM) model and PI-section simulations, which represent fundamentally different approaches. The analysis reveals that sheath circulating currents in the sea-to-land transition section increased by a factor of up to 1.8 compared to the undisturbed three-core submarine cable configuration. This increase caused the maximum conductor temperatures to exceed 100 °C, far more than the 90 °C operational limit for XLPE insulation. The study addresses practical mitigation strategies for end effects in submarine cable installations and addresses a critical gap in existing methods for rating calculations of submarine power cables.

title: Reduction of Arc-Induced Mechanical Stress on a 1000 kV Power Transformer Tank Through Embedded High-Voltage Lead Exit Design
abstract: The high-voltage lead exit is installed in a compact turret external to a 1000 kV power transformer tank. Strong shock waves induced by high-energy arc faults in the lead exit pose a serious risk to turret and tank safety. To enhance the arc withstand capability of 1000 kV power transformer tanks, this study proposes a novel embedded high-voltage lead exit design. Compared to traditional configurations, the enlarged embedded lead exit facilitates the dispersion and attenuation of arc-induced pressure waves, thereby reducing the risk of explosion and combustion. A comprehensive evaluation—including electric field distribution, mechanical strength, and explosion resistance—is conducted to validate the structural reliability and arc fault tolerance of the proposed design. Notably, an arc pressure simulation method based on the bubble pulsation approach is introduced, in which actual arc power is injected into a gas volume equivalent to the arc length to model the pressure source. The Johnson–Cook (JC) failure criterion is employed to accurately evaluate material failure. Simulation results confirm that the embedded configuration significantly enhances arc fault resistance under various internal fault scenarios. This novel design offers a practical solution for improving the safety and reliability of ultra-high-voltage (UHV) transformers and provides valuable insights for optimizing high-voltage lead exit structures in critical applications.

title: Structural Design and Performance Optimization of Flexible Connection Structure of On-Load Tap Changer Under Transient Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Coupling
abstract: On-load tap changers (OLTCs) rely on flexible connection structures (FCSs) to maintain conductive circuits between moveable contacts. Stress concentration represents a primary cause of FCS mechanical failure, yet its behavior under transient electro-thermo-mechanical coupling conditions remains insufficiently addressed. This study develops a shape optimization method based on parametric curves and adaptive optimization to mitigate stress concentration in FCSs. Transient coupling stress analyses are performed for both fixed and moveable FCS types, and geometry-specific parametric curves are constructed according to the identified stress concentration locations and their underlying causes. Adaptive parameter optimization yields significant stress reductions in both cases. The analysis is further extended to multiple consecutive switching cycles, providing a more realistic assessment of FCS stress evolution under actual OLTC service conditions.

title: A Full-Cycle Model of the AC Electric Arc Furnace Considering the Production Process
abstract: The existing electric arc furnace models mainly focus on the power quality issues generated during the melting period, failing to fully consider that the smelting process is a continuous and dynamic one. This results in the lack of a complete full-cycle model of the electric arc furnace, thereby restricting the assessment of power quality throughout the entire smelting process. Therefore, this paper proposes a full-cycle model of the AC electric arc furnace considering the production process. Firstly, by analyzing the influence of the production process on the furnace gas during the steelmaking process of the electric arc furnace, the dynamic mapping relationship between the gas concentration changing with time and the microscopic particle behavior in the arc was revealed using the electronic continuity equation. Secondly, based on the magnetic compression force balance equation, the quantitative relationship between pressure and radius was derived, and the function of the arc length change throughout the cycle was constructed. Thirdly, through a combination of mechanism and data, the gas concentration change curves and the arc length change functions for each stage of the smelting process were determined. Finally, using a 55-ton steelmaking AC electric arc furnace as the research object, a model was established on the Matlab/Simulink platform to verify its accuracy. The simulation results show that the proposed model is consistent with the actual production process of the AC electric arc furnace and can accurately reflect the entire power quality cycle of the entire period.

title: Research on Vibration Characteristics of Amorphous Alloy Three-Dimensional Wound Core Transformer Considering Insulating Oil
abstract: Amorphous alloy transformer has energy-saving advantages, but its magnetostrictive effect is higher than that of silicon steel transformer, causing severe vibration and noise, which makes it very easy for amorphous alloy debris to be produced, thereby leading to insulation faults. Additionally, transformer is important power equipment for power delivery. Therefore, in order to reflect the vibration information of the core under different external environments, an analysis model for the transmission of core vibration to the tank is established, to analyze the vibration characteristics of the tank of the amorphous alloy 3D wound core transformer under both insulating oil and non-insulating oil conditions. Firstly, to obtain fundamental magnetization and magnetostriction characteristics, a single-frame amorphous alloy three-dimensional wound (3D) core magnetic property testing platform is constructed. Subsequently, drawing on the principles of elastic mechanics, a magneto-mechanical coupled vibration model is established for amorphous alloy 3D wound core. Meanwhile, a vibration test platform is constructed to obtain the distribution trend of core vibration under different operating conditions, which the accuracy of the finite element model for core vibration is validated. Finally, the investigation is carried on a 50 kVA amorphous alloy wound 3D transformer to evaluate tank’s vibration characteristics under the conditions with and without insulating oil, obtaining vibration intensity and frequency distribution characteristics of the tank, and the accuracy of the tank’s vibration characteristics is validated for transformer model. On this basis, the influence of insulating oil temperature on the tank’s vibration characteristics is considered to reveal the relationship among the vibration characteristics of insulating oil, core, and tank. To break through the limitations of traditional electrical detection methods and provide a theoretical basis for the online fault diagnosis of core.

title: A Novel Eigenvalue Structure for Two-Mode Resonance Stability Analysis: SSCIs Between Wind Generation and Power Systems as Examples
abstract: Intensified interactions among diversified devices, especially those for wind generation, have caused many events of subsynchronous control interactions (SSCIs) and posed a challenge to power system stability. It is hard for the classical modal analysis to quantify the interaction among oscillation modes explicitly and explain why the interaction or resonance occurs, because eigenvalues and eigenvectors are not differentiable at the resonance point and move drastically nearby. This paper proposes a novel inherence-interaction eigenvalue structure that manages to extend classical single-mode analysis to two-mode resonance stability and SSCI analysis. In the proposed structure, slow-varying inherent eigenvalues denoting properties of two modes themselves and quantities reflecting their interaction are detached. Hence, the SSCI instability mechanism can be ascribed to and explicitly quantified by damping exchange between two modes under interaction. Variation of the oscillation frequency and eigenvectors can be explained likewise. The proposed theory is used to explain SSCI mechanism between wind generation and power systems, and accurately predict rapidly-changing eigenvalues as well as construct the SSCI stability region under parameter variation. The effectiveness is validated by results on two typical systems and the New England 39-bus system, compared with several existing methods.

title: Stray Current Mitigation With Reverse Running Rail Current Control Strategy for Virtual-Return-Based DC Traction Power Supply System
abstract: The virtual-return-based DC traction power supply system (VRTPS) has been studied to solve the stray current and rail potential issues in urban rail transit. By utilizing the power electronic devices (PEDs) and return line, VRTPS constructs the zero-resistance virtual return path (VRP) by diverting traction current from the running rail into this newly established path. However, the mitigation performance of existing VRTPS control strategies is still suboptimal, leading to incomplete suppression of stray current and rail potential within the train-occupied section. Thus, the reverse running rail current control strategy of VRTPS is proposed to further reduce the stray current and rail potential. Firstly, the topology and modeling of VRTPS are investigated to analyze the inherent limitations of the ideal zero-resistance VRP. Secondly, the detailed analysis of the reverse running rail current control for VRTPS is presented, which optimizes the running rail current distribution with the variable-resistance VRP. Thirdly, the comparative researches on both the stray current and rail potential distribution are conducted between the conventional system and VRTPS with different control strategies. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of VRTPS with proposed strategy on the stray current and rail potential mitigation are validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: Effect of IBR Negative-Sequence Control on Phase-to-Phase Fault Direction Determination
abstract: Protective relays implement algorithms to determine the direction to the fault. Phase-to-phase fault detection, can rely on negative sequence components. If the negative sequence currents provided by an inverter-based resource (IBR) are not reliable, the directional determination of the fault is not consistent. In this paper, we compare two types of IBRs: grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM), for their dynamic performance when subject to phase-to-phase faults on the high side of the step-up transformer. The GFL-IBR behaves as a positive-sequence current source, while the GFM-IBR behaves as a voltage source behind an inductive impedance in the positive-sequence circuit, and as an inductive impedance in the negative-sequence circuit. It is found that the GFM-IBR ensures proper fault ride-through, while the GFL-IBR cannot ride through such a fault. Additionally, the GFM-IBR ensures correct fault detection via negative-sequence directionality check, while this check fails for the GFL-IBR case. Therefore, the GFM design presented in this paper appears to have two advantages compared to the legacy GFL design: better capability of fault ride-through and assurance of correct fault direction determination.

title: Contour Optimization of DC-GIS Insulator Considering the Influence of Surface Charging Withstanding Transient Voltages
abstract: Surface charging on insulator in DC-GIS is influenced by transient voltages like lightning impulse (LI) and polarity reversal (PR), which threatens the safe operation of the equipment. In this paper, a contour optimization method considering the influence of surface charging is proposed for insulator used in DC-GIS of ±320 kV. The insulation reliability under steady DC voltage is promoted, and the property to withstand the transient voltages is guaranteed as well. The normal and tangential components of electric field under steady DC voltage are simultaneously minimized, and the constraints on electric field under the transient voltages are incorporated. The results show that, under the steady DC voltage, the maximal value of normal electric field is reduced by 5.8%, and the tangential field is simultaneously reduced by 7.0% on the insulator with the optimal contour after optimization. The maximal values of electric fields under the LI and PR voltages are 8.82 and 3.49 kV/mm, respectively, meeting the insulation requirements. It is suggested that, the proposed method incorporating the property withstanding the LI and PR voltages yields a more reliable performance of the optimized insulator in DC-GIS.

title: Fault Analysis and Pilot Protection Scheme for Various Single-Phase Line Breaks in Resonant Grounding Systems
abstract: Due to small fault currents and different fault characteristics under various grounding types on both sides of the fault point, the existing methods are facing challenges in the analysis and protection principle for single-phase break faults (SPBFs) in resonant grounding systems (RGSs), including inaccurate fault identification, low sensitivity, and insufficient reliability under high-impedance grounding and intermittent arc faults. In this paper, fault characteristics of zero-sequence voltages upstream and downstream of the break point with different grounding modes are analyzed. The SPBFs with grounding at single-side and without grounding only exhibit the amplitude or phase characteristic, while SPBFs with grounding at both sides incorporate the two features. On this basis, a pilot protection scheme is developed for various SPBFs in RGSs, where internal and external SPBFs are determined by combining the features of the amplitude and phase of dual-terminal zero-sequence voltages. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology is validated through a closed-loop hardware test by applying a real-time digital simulator (RTDS) and the developed protective devices. Experimental results prove that the protection scheme performs well under different fault types, fault locations, fault resistances, and the presence of inverter-interfaced distributed generators.

title: Vibration-Based Detection of Cable Bending in Cable GIS Terminations via Experimental Measurements and Interface Stress Simulation
abstract: Cable GIS terminations are prone to insulation defects induced by abnormal internal stress and strain, due to their complex internal structure, latent defects, and sensitivity to installation quality. One typical manifestation of such abnormal mechanical states is internal cable bending, whose influence on the vibration response of cable GIS terminations remains insufficiently understood. To address this issue, this study proposes a vibration-based method for detecting abnormal stress-strain conditions at insulation interfaces, enabling early identification of hidden insulation defects. First, vibration theory and simulation models are combined to examine how internal cable bending influences interfacial insulation pressure and the corresponding vibration response. Subsequently, a vibration testing platform for 110-kV cable GIS terminations is established to measure and analyze the vibration characteristics under normal and simulated abnormal stress-strain conditions, with the latter induced by cable bending. Finally, the vibration characteristics are evaluated using time-domain and frequency-domain indicators. The results demonstrate that internal cable bending leads to non-uniform stress distributions at the insulation interfaces between the bushing, stress cone, and cable. The cable-end vibration, which is typically the most pronounced under normal conditions, is significantly suppressed, accompanied by a noticeable shift of the vibration signal toward the lower-frequency domain and an increase in damping. These findings establish a vibration response characterization framework for cable bending defects and provide a basis for non-intrusive condition assessment of cable GIS terminations.

title: Transient Voltage and Current Calculations Based on Formulation of Modified Baum-Liu-Tesche Equation in Phase Domain
abstract: This study presents a modified Baum-Liu-Tesche (BLT) equation, derived in a compact matrix-algebraic form, for the frequency-domain analysis of transient voltages and currents in multi-conductor transmission lines (MTLs). The proposed formulation addresses two broad categories of transient events, including faults and lightning strikes, while accommodating diverse event types and occurrence scenarios. The modified BLT equation is further extended into an explicit form, enabling its application to power networks with inhomogeneous parameters and complex topologies. This extension is supported by a systematic derivation of the structural features and element characteristics of the involved matrices and vectors. Numerical validation using the benchmark IEEE 34-bus test distribution network confirms strong agreement between the results obtained from the modified BLT equation and those generated by electromagnetic-transient-type simulations. Overall, the proposed formulation provides an effective and robust analytical framework for transient analysis in power systems.

title: Impedance-Spectrum Driven Frequency-Weighted Functional Fault Location in Undersea Observation Network Power Systems
abstract: Fault location in the power supply systems of undersea observation networks is constrained by limited observability and the frequency-dependent characteristics of the electrode–seawater–cable loop. This paper proposes a frequency-domain fault location method based on impedance spectrum analysis, in which the identification of fault parameters is formulated as a minimization problem of a frequency-weighted residual functional. A physical model of the electrode–cable–fault path is constructed to compute theoretical input impedance spectra under different fault distances and fault impedances. These spectra are then compared to the measured impedance spectrum obtained at the shore station under swept-frequency excitation. The residual functional is constructed by separating the real and imaginary components of the spectral difference, reflecting the deviation of complex input impedance at each frequency point. Considering the influence of impedance sensitivity across frequencies, independent weighting functions are introduced for the real and imaginary components to enhance contributions from informative bands and suppress unreliable regions. This yields a frequency-weighted residual functional with physical significance, characterizing the correspondence between fault parameters and spectral discrepancy. The functional is minimized via a gradient-based optimization strategy, enabling simultaneous determination of fault distance and fault impedance based solely on shore-side measurements. Simulation studies across various fault conditions validate the method's performance in terms of location accuracy, robustness under high impedance scenarios, and numerical stability over long transmission distances. The proposed framework fuses spectral sensitivity with physical transmission modeling to infer spatial fault characteristics solely from frequency-domain observations, without relying on internal measurements or reflectometry.

title: A Physics-Informed Topology-Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network for Harmonic Source Location in Three-Phase Distribution Networks With Renewable Energy Integration
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources has led to a significant increase in the number of harmonic sources within distribution networks. Concurrently, the altered supply modes introduced by renewable integration have caused dynamic changes in the network topology. Therefore, this paper proposes a three-phase distribution network harmonic source location method based on a physics-informed topology adaptive graph convolutional network. Firstly, a harmonic pseudo-measurement method based on emission characteristics modelling is developed to address the shortage of harmonic measurements. Secondly, considering the dynamic changes in the distribution network topology, a multi-layer perception topology adaptive graph convolutional neural network is proposed, which is used to establish the mapping relationship between harmonic measurements and state variables. Meanwhile, the harmonic transfer equation and system parameters are embedded into the neural network training as physical constraints to ensure the results conform to physical properties. Then, a harmonic source identification criterion is established, and the long-term statistical index derived from the estimated harmonic injection current is used to locate harmonic sources in the distribution network. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified in the IEEE 37-bus system and the actual system.

title: Degradation, Lifetime, and Failure Modes of Metal Oxide Varistors in Low-Voltage DC Circuit Breaker Applications
abstract: The metal oxide varistor (MOV) has been a critical enabling component for emerging applications in low-voltage dc circuit breakers (LVDCCBs). Although its properties align well with this application, its long-term performance, including degradation, failure modes, and service lifetime, remains poorly understood. Based on an accelerated degradation test (ADT) platform, this work collects extensive data to track degradation patterns and identify failure modes using statistical methods. A power-function-based model is proposed to identify the driving forces behind degradation, and a complete lifetime map of LVDCCB MOVs is achieved. The model predicts the lifetime of LVDCCB MOVs with a confidence level of 79.18%. The model and statistical analysis indicate that charge is the driving force for the defined failure mode, which needs to be addressed in the LVDCCB design while energy drives the catastrophic failure mode, which needs to be avoided in the LVDCCB design.

title: Multiple Regulation Phase Shifting Transformer: A Flexible and High-Accuracy Power Flow Controller
abstract: With the increasing share of renewable energy in modern power systems, the power grid urgently needs effective power flow regulation technology. The phase shifting transformer has the advantages of strong power flow regulation capability, low investment, high reliability, but the traditional phase shifting transformer can only realize discrete regulation, with low regulation accuracy and lack of appropriate amplitude regulation capability. Therefore, this paper proposes a multiple regulating phase shifting transformer (MR-PST) and its design scheme for power system, analyzes its input and output characteristics based on its topology, examines the nature and distribution of its compensation voltage, and establishes boundary equations from the constraints of single amplitude regulation and dual phase regulation, proving that this structure can effectively increase the number of regulation points, increase the regulation accuracy, introduce the amplitude regulation capability, and optimize the regulation region. Then the power flow regulation region is quantitatively analyzed, and the extremum expression and boundary calculation method of power flow regulation range under different conditions are obtained. Finally, the rationality and practicality of MR-PST were verified through virtual simulation and physical experiments.

title: Quasi-Steady-State Frequency Based ROCOF Relay Realisation for Secured LOM Protection
abstract: Rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) relay is widely used to detect loss of main (LoM) events. RoCoF is commonly calculated using the frequency estimated through phase-locked loop (PLL). These relays monitor the RoCoF and initiate tripping when predefined thresholds are exceeded. However, PLL-based frequency estimators are prone to producing erroneous RoCoF measurements during transient system conditions, leading to unnecessary source disconnection despite the system remaining within ride-through limits. This paper uses the concept of a geometric definition of frequency to calculate RoCoF and assert its validity during transients. The proposed logic can help in improving the security of the RoCoF relay and prevent undesired tripping of distributed generation compared to PLL based logic.

title: Hybrid Grid-Forming Control for Enhanced Active Support and DC Voltage Stability in MMC-HVDC Systems
abstract: Grid-forming control based on power synchronization and DC voltage synchronization is two typical approaches for enabling modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems to operate in weak grids. However, the inherent limitations of their synchronization mechanisms make it difficult to simultaneously ensure system stability and economic efficiency. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a two-stage hybrid grid-forming control strategy. In the first stage, a decoupled matching control is designed to exploit the energy stored in submodule (SM) capacitors for active damping support, which achieves nonlinear indirect matching between DC voltage and frequency while maintaining the economic operation of the sending-end grid. Meanwhile, a voltage stabilization method based on redundant SMs is proposed to decouple SM capacitor voltage from the DC voltage, thereby enhancing DC voltage stability. In the second stage, once the average voltage of the SMs exceeds a predefined threshold, virtual synchronous generator control mobilizes the reserved energy from renewable plants and the rotor kinetic energy of wind turbines, further strengthening inertia and damping support. Moreover, a small-signal model is developed to reveal the parameter evolution, and a unified two-stage framework is established through control correction and parameter optimization, thereby improving system dynamic performance and stability. Finally, PSCAD/EMTDC simulations validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Transient Voltage Stability Analysis and Enhancement of Grid-Following Converters Considering DC-link Voltage Control Dynamics
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy resources through grid-following converters, the voltage support capability of the system is weakened, thereby increasing the risk of voltage instability. Existing studies mainly focus on the transient voltage stability of induction motors (IMs), where the dynamics of voltage source converters (VSCs) are often neglected. However, VSCs with DC-link voltage control (DVC) also face the risk of transient voltage instability under grid faults, even when the voltage-supporting effect of VSCs during low-voltage ride through (LVRT) is considered. Such an instability phenomenon poses a tremendous threat to the stable operation of VSC-dominated power systems, which has not been addressed in existing research. To fill this gap, this paper provides a theoretical explanation of the VSC’s transient performance under DVC and LVRT, and reveals the transient voltage instability mechanism of modern power systems with high penetration of VSCs. To mitigate such instability, this paper proposes an adaptive current-limiting control strategy after analyzing the impact of current limitation on transient voltage stability. Simulation results verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

title: A Unified Probability Model for Multi-Type Power Quality Disturbances Based on Operating States Identification
abstract: The Grid-connected inverter (GCI) inevitably generates the multi-type power quality disturbances at the same time; for example, it not only emits harmonic currents but also causes voltage fluctuations. Building one model to describe the multi-type disturbances is necessary for disturbance source tracing, disturbance prediction, mitigation decision, and so on. This study proposes a unified probability model for multi-type power quality disturbances for GCI based on operating states identification. Firstly, it proposes an operating states identification algorithm considering multi-type disturbances, to facilitate the construction of the disturbance model for different operating states. Secondly, the unified probability model for multi-type power quality disturbances is developed, which includes the edge probability model and unified probability model, to analyze the occurrence probability and coupling relationship of multi-type disturbances. Finally, the accuracy and validity of the proposed method are verified by using the real recorded data of photovoltaic (PV) GCI in practice.

title: Probabilistic Multi-Objective Design of Lightning Protection for Complex Power Distribution Networks
abstract: Some of the main issues in developing an effective lightning protection strategy include determining the optimal placement of protection devices and deciding whether to incorporate shield wires. Addressing these challenges involves balancing multiple, often conflicting, objectives. Additionally, the intrinsic probabilistic nature of the lightning problem makes the optimization even more complicated. Based on the above considerations, this study proposes a multi-objective optimization framework to identify effective lightning protection strategies, in terms of surge arrester location and shield wire installation in complex distribution networks. The proposed approach aims to find a computationally efficient procedure that preserves the accuracy of conventional methods, even in complex network configurations. This is accomplished by integrating decision theory with a Design of Experiments approach based on Taguchi arrays to determine the optimal protection alternative. This method allows obtaining substantial reduction of the computational time. The computational time reduction depends on the network complexity and on the configuration of the reference method. In the simulations presented in this paper, the proposed approach allowed reducing computational time up to approximately 98% compared to a benchmark method based on genetic algorithm combined with the Monte Carlo technique, while preserving the accuracy of the results. The proposed method offers a practical and scalable solution for enhancing lightning resilience despite the complexity of the distribution networks' topology.

title: Line Equivalent Based Short-Circuit Current Calculation in Distribution Networks With Numerous Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generators
abstract: The calculation of short-circuit current (SCC) is crucial for planning, operation and maintenance of distribution systems. The integration of Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Generators (IIDGs) into distribution systems induces nonlinear characteristics, which make the traditional nodal voltage equation-based SCC calculation methods ineffective. To balance the SCC calculation accuracy and efficiency, a line equivalent based SCC calculation method is proposed to address the increasing integration of IIDGs in distribution networks. Firstly, an aggregation zoning method for IIDGs is proposed based on their fault response characteristics. Both the Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) controlling and fault steady-state voltage drop are considered. Then, an equivalent model of the non-fault line, utilizing piecewise equivalence, is established to simplify the network structure. Finally, the post-fault node voltages and branch currents are determined by solving the nodal voltage equation of the established simplified network with fixed-point iteration. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed algorithm has satisfactory accuracy and computation time in calculating SCC of distribution networks with numerous IIDGs.

title: Different-Frequency Differential Protection Method of Adjustable Speed Hydro-Generating Unit Based on Fixed Characteristic Frequency Band
abstract: During the operation of Adjustable speed hydro-generating unit (ASHU), due to high speed and large centrifugal force, the rotor winding is easily squeezed and causes short-circuit fault. The development of a reliable protection scheme is imperative. As a new and potential method, the universality of different-frequency differential protection is still limited under wide speed operation conditions. Therefore, a rotor winding short-circuit protection method based on fixed characteristic frequency band is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the internal relationship between the harmonic characteristics of rotor current and slip rate in the case of winding short-circuit fault of ASHU is analyzed. On this basis, the construction method of different-frequency differential current protection criterion based on fixed characteristic frequency band is proposed. Furthermore, combined with the waveform of the dynamic simulation experiment, the Generalized S Transform (GST) is used to carry out time-frequency analysis. The feasibility of the construction approach of the protection criterion is verified. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed protection method is suitable for the wide speed operation condition of ASHU. It can achieve fast action under rotor winding short-circuit fault (RWSF), and has high selectivity under stator winding short-circuit fault (SWSF), which can effectively avoid protection misoperation.

title: Analysis of Lightning-Elevated Structures Interaction in Tropical Regions and Implications for Wind Turbine Risk Assessment
abstract: This study analyzes the lightning interaction with elevated structures (ES) in a high-lightning activity region of central Colombia by integrating Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) observations with LINET cloud-to-ground stroke data. In addition, the annual number of lightning flashes (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) to ES is determined directly from LINET measurements and compared with the obtain using the expression of NTC 4552-2:2023, IEC 62305-2:2024, and the Eriksson equation. The same analysis is extended to two wind farms in northern Colombia, where <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula> for wind turbines is evaluated following the IEC 61400-24:2018 standard. LMA observations show that all CG strokes affecting ES are initiated by downward leaders and influenced by the lower positive charge region (LPCR) in thunderstorms. Likewise, positive leaders exhibited significantly longer paths than negative leaders. Analysis of <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula> reveals two exposure regimes: in low-activity regions, structural height governs <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, whereas in high-activity zones the ground flash density (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_G}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) becomes the dominant factor, particularly for ES below 70 m. In general, the <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula> values obtained from LINET exceed those predicted by the normative formulations. However, using ground strike-point density (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_G}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) values derived directly from the lightning location system (LLS) substantially improves the agreement between calculated and observed <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{N}_D}$</tex-math></inline-formula> values, particularly for tall structures and wind turbines, thereby avoiding the underestimation of lightning-related design parameters such as the risk components.

title: Reduced-Scale Test Method for Dynamic Responses of Bundle Conductor Line Following Ice-Shedding
abstract: A reduced-scale test method for dynamic responses of bundle conductor line following ice-shedding is proposed. In this method, hollow cylindrical electromagnets are used to absorb and release mass blocks modelling ice on and ice-shedding from sub-conductors, multiple cameras are utilized to capture the vertical, transverse and torsional vibrations, tension sensors to measure tensions in all sub-conductors, and three-component force sensors to measure the reaction force at hanging points. Without simplifying the bundle conductor line into a single one which was employed in previous works, the proposed reduced-scale model can satisfy the similarities of bending and torsion stiffness at the same time, model the torsional vibration induced by ice-shedding from sub-conductors, and record tension in each sub-conductor. Reduced-scale test platform for a twin-bundle conductor line was established and utilized to study the dynamic characteristics of the twin-bundle conductor line following partial, unzipping and asynchronous ice-shedding from sub-conductors. The method can be extended to investigate dynamic characteristics of bundle conductor lines following any pattern of ice-shedding.

title: Sequential Switching Modeling and Transient Instability Mechanism for MMC-HVDC Receiving-End Systems With Fault Ride-Through
abstract: Previous literature shows that the second-order phase-locked loop dynamics dominate the transient stability of high voltage direct current system based on modular multilevel converter (MMC-HVDC) in the during-fault stage. The effects of DC-link dynamics and transient behavior after fault recovery have rarely been studied. Focusing on the post-fault stage, this paper first develops a transient model in each fault stage based on the typical fault ride-through strategy, considering the DC-link voltage dynamics. Although the during-fault stage is stable, the MMC-HVDC system still faces the risk of transient instability in the post-fault stage under receiving-end AC weak grid faults because of DC voltage deviation. The angular frequency jumps that occur in both the during-fault stage and post-fault stage are uncovered. High-dimensional basin-of-attraction analysis reveals that the angular frequency jump generated by the DC-link voltage dynamics can weaken the resynchronization capability. Moreover, based on the proposed transient stability margin index, the parameter feasible region under different ramp coefficients, DC voltage droop coefficients, and short circuit ratios is obtained. Finally, hardware-in-the-loop experiments are conducted to validate the results of the theoretical analysis.

title: Energy storage-empowered multi-type EV charging infrastructure for power-constrained buildings: A two-stage design optimization framework
abstract: Large-scale deployment of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure in existing commercial buildings is often constrained by limited transformer capacity, particularly in high-density cities where electrical upgrades are costly and difficult to implement. To address this challenge, this study investigates the technical and economic feasibility of using energy storage systems (ESSs) to support EV charger deployment in power-constrained buildings. A two-stage design optimization framework is proposed to co-optimize EV charger deployment and ESS energy and power capacities. The upper-level design optimization uses a genetic algorithm to search for the optimal configuration of multi-type EV chargers and the ESS while satisfying users' basic commuting requirements. The lower-level operation optimization then determines the optimal ESS scheduling that minimizes operational cost under the transformer capacity constraint. The results show that the proposed framework significantly increases the achievable EV penetration in power-constrained buildings without requiring electrical upgrades, while substantially improving life-cycle economic performance. Compared with conventional single-type charger deployment supported by electrical upgrades, the proposed framework substantially reduces life-cycle cost by 43.1–175.5% while achieving higher charging quality of service. Overall, this study provides a technically feasible and cost-effective planning pathway for enabling high EV penetration in existing power-constrained buildings, thereby facilitating transport electrification in high-density cities.

title: Integration of linear and metaheuristic optimization for state estimation in low voltage distribution grids
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for state estimation in low-voltage (LV) distribution grids with limited access to real-time measurement data, combining the methodologies of two novel approaches and introducing a new hybrid integration. First, we introduce a linear programming optimization (LPO) approach for unbalanced three-phase state estimation, which efficiently estimates nodal injections using historical data and sparse real time measurements while minimizing computational complexity. Second, we propose a three-stage hybrid metaheuristic optimization (HMO) framework that includes node level forecasting of active and reactive power, phase level disaggregation of aggregated forecasts, and voltage estimation via a hybrid metaheuristic optimization scheme. Finally, we propose an integrated linear metaheuristic framework (ILMF ) in which the linear optimization solution serves as an initial condition for the metaheuristic framework, enabling faster convergence and improved accuracy. To move beyond a purely warm-start integration, the ILMF further incorporates an Adaptive Sensitivity Refresh (ASR) mechanism that recomputes the voltage sensitivities online whenever the operating point drifts beyond an empirically validated range, so that the refinement is always guided by locally valid sensitivities rather than a single fixed linearization. Based on the results, LPO offers high computational efficiency, while HMO achieves higher estimation accuracy. The proposed ILMF effectively balances accuracy and computational performance. In particular, ILMF is validated on real LV grids in Denmark, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.15 V, a standard deviation of 1.40 V, and a root mean square error of 1.48 V. Rather than dominating on every metric, the proposed framework is positioned as offering a favourable accuracy–stability trade-off: it consistently reduces the worst-case (maximum) error and the estimation variance while remaining competitive on mean error, and it is more resilient than the purely metaheuristic approach under reduced observability. These results demonstrate that the proposed multi-stage framework successfully combines forecasting, linear optimization, and metaheuristic refinement, leading to improved accuracy, robustness, and observability in real low-voltage distribution feeders, with a computational structure that scales linearly per evaluation with network size (validation on larger standard feeders is identified as future work).

title: Hierarchical operation optimization of reserve storage capacity in pumped-storage power stations for enhanced high-penetration renewable energy accommodation
abstract: Pumped-storage power (PSP) stations play a vital role in promoting renewable energy accommodation, yet the operational potential of their reserve storage capacity (RSC) remains insufficiently exploited. This study proposes a hierarchical control framework for RSC in PSP peak-shaving and valley-filling operation, coordinating hydropower benefit and mitigating residual load fluctuation (RLF) while contributing to carbon emission reduction. The framework is implemented through a multi-objective operation model and applied to the Heimifeng PSP station in Hunan, China, under diverse equivalent load scenarios. Results reveal distinct allocation characteristics between the two reservoirs: preferred lower-reservoir RSC allocations are concentrated within 1–4%, whereas upper-reservoir RSC varies over a broader 1–7% range under different operating conditions. The coordinated operation scheme therefore achieves a compromise between hydropower benefit enhancement and residual load fluctuation mitigation. Under Scenario S3 in spring, the hydropower benefit reaches USD 22.92 million, while RLF is reduced by approximately 8% compared with fixed RSC control. Carbon emission reductions are achieved under all 12 load season conditions, with the maximum improvement reaching approximately 24% under Scenario S2 in winter. The proposed hierarchical RSC control framework enables scenario-adaptive RSC allocation and provides a practical approach for improving peak-shaving performance and hydropower benefits under high renewable energy penetration.

title: Compound deployment risk analysis in direct air capture, green ammonia and long-duration energy storage
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC), green ammonia and long-duration energy storage (LDES) projects have attracted large public commitments, yet project cancellations are mounting. This paper argues that deployment fails when several barriers bind at once, chiefly absent demand, uncompetitive cost, policy uncertainty and unbankable finance, and that a technology's prospects are set by its weakest barrier rather than its average strength. That logic is formalised in a Compound Deployment Risk Index, stress-tested for robustness, and paired with a levelised-cost model for each technology, using sourced data through mid-2026. The results show why each technology stalls. Capturing CO2 from air costs 480–1000 USD per tonne, more than any compliance scheme currently pays. Green ammonia becomes competitive as a shipping fuel only at a carbon penalty of 370 to 680 USD per tonne, above the 100 to 380 USD proposed by the International Maritime Organization. Furthermore, in Great Britain's storage auction, new battery chemistries were undercut by lithium-ion and pumped hydro at every procured duration. The policy conclusion is that creating demand is necessary but not sufficient: it must be paired with cost reduction and de-risked finance for a self-sustaining industry to emerge.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis: Cradle-to-gate supply chain emissions and scale-dependent cost analysis
abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of anion exchange membrane electrolysis that combines experimentally validated lifecycle inventory data, comprehensive cradle-to-gate greenhouse gas accounting, and probabilistic techno-economic analysis under scale-dependent conditions. The results demonstrate that under a realistic Net Zero 2050 grid scenario, the total carbon footprint is estimated at 2.53 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , with electricity consumption dominating the environmental impact. However, evaluating the system under an ideal zero‑carbon electricity supply reveals a baseline footprint of 0.44 kgCO 2 eq/kgH 2 , demonstrating that upstream material production and component manufacturing impose an irreducible minimum emission threshold. Economically, the levelized cost of hydrogen decreases from $8.16/kgH 2 at a production scale of 1,000 kgH 2 /day to $5.05/kgH 2 at 50,000 kgH 2 /day, driven primarily by economies of scale. Notably, the two-parameter interaction analysis reveals that system availability and electrochemical efficiency act as primary co-optimization drivers, exhibiting a pronounced synergistic interaction for global warming potential while delivering additive economic benefits for hydrogen production cost. Furthermore, increasing system scale not only lowers costs but also progressively narrows economic uncertainty. These findings highlight that the sustainability of green hydrogen cannot be accurately evaluated without incorporating upstream supply chain impacts alongside operational metrics. The study provides an evidence-based framework for evaluating emerging electrolysis technologies and informing rigorous carbon certification standards.

title: Amygdala beta bursts modulate hippocampal neuronal dynamics during human emotional processing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The amygdala and hippocampus are key structures in emotional processing, yet the transient neural dynamics coordinating their interaction remain poorly understood. We simultaneously recorded single-neuron activity and local field potentials from these regions in epilepsy patients performing an emotional image-rating task. Neurons in both regions exhibited firing rate changes predictive of subjective emotional valence. While conventional spectral analysis revealed no valence-specific patterns, beta bursts (13-30 Hz)–transient, high-power events–were selectively modified by task features. In both regions, beta bursts were associated with increased gamma amplitude and enhanced phase coherence, with beta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling capturing emotion-related dynamics. Critically, amygdala beta bursts were associated with valence-dependent, bidirectional modulation of hippocampal interneuron firing – decreased during very unpleasant/highest arousal processing and increased during high-arousal very pleasant processing – while putative pyramidal-cell firing did not change significantly. Hippocampal bursts showed no reciprocal influence. These findings suggest that beta bursts may represent a temporally precise neural correlate of emotional appraisal and a potential target for neuromodulation in mood disorders.

title: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reverting waste carbon into chemicals and materials with minimal freshwater reliance is essential for a sustainable future. Here, we report the establishment of a blue biological scheme by repurposing the evolutionary fitness of the marine bacterium Roseovarius nubinhibens for efficient conversion of lignin-derived carbon into valuable chemicals with seawater as a water source. We create independency of the superior catalytic capacity of R. nubinhibens to circumvent a rare polar effect, and genetically decouple the bioproduction pathway from central metabolism, channeling all lignin-derived carbon into desired products. Next, an orthogonal growth module is generated with acetate as a second carbon source, which is a ubiquitous byproduct and inhibitor in plant biomass hydrolysis, to sustain cell growth and supply necessary resources, but not substrates, for the growth-coupled bioproduction. Besides this designed metabolic segregation, we identify a cross-module push-and-pull synergy between bioproduction and cell growth, enabling enhanced performance and robustness. By deploying this biological scheme, we successfully achieve escalated conversion of the lignin-derived monomer 4-hydroxybenzoate to value-added compounds protocatechuate and β-ketoadipate with seawater, rather than freshwater, as the water source, generating a distinct blue biological scheme with potential for simultaneous carbon and water conservation.

title: PrimPol toggled by ATR modulates fork slowing and repriming under oncogenic KRAS-induced replication stress
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: During the early phases of oncogenic clonal expansion, precancerous cells experience replication stress that threatens both genomic integrity and viability. How replication stress tolerance (RST) mechanisms are dynamically reprogrammed across the different stages of cancer progression remains elusive. Here, we identify PrimPol as a central regulator that executes two fundamentally distinct RST modes in response to oncogenic KRAS-induced heterochromatin-associated replication stress (K-HaRS). Unexpectedly, during acute K-HaRS, an unphosphorylated form of PrimPol cooperates with the fork remodeler SMARCAL1 to actively slow fork progression, stabilizing challenged forks and limiting engagement of error-prone DNA synthesis. As K-HaRS persists, PrimPol undergoes an ATR-dependent functional switch, whereby its phosphorylated form promotes repriming while fork slowing is attenuated, enabling replication to proceed across heterochromatin barriers despite persistent stress. Strikingly, loss of PrimPol enforces chronic reliance on the error-prone Rev1-Polζ-dependent synthesis and compromises cellular fitness under KRAS-driven stress. Thus, these findings establish PrimPol as a context-dependent regulator of RST that, through ATR-dependent toggling of its functional modes, coordinates fork slowing and repriming to safeguard replication fork stability while permitting an optimal compromise of genome stability that would fuel oncogenic clonal evolution.

title: Substrate coupling and inhibition in human Na+-dependent Cl−/HCO3− exchanger NCBE (SLC4A10)
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Maintaining pH homoeostasis is essential for neuronal excitability and for regulating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The Na⁺-dependent Cl⁻/HCO3⁻ exchanger, NCBE (SLC4A10), abundant in the choroid plexus, contributes to CSF pH control by mediating bicarbonate flux, yet its molecular mechanism has remained unclear. Here we report cryo-EM structures of human NCBE in multiple functional states, revealing conserved binding sites for Na⁺, Cl⁻, and HCO3⁻, as well as an unexpected K⁺ site indicating relaxed cation selectivity. The inhibitor DIDS binds above the substrate cavity, locking NCBE in an outward-facing conformation and defining a subfamily-selective inhibitory mechanism. Functional assays and molecular dynamics simulations support the coordination of ions and the inhibitory effects. Comparison with an AlphaFold3-predicted inward-facing model suggests an elevator-like transport mechanism and delineates the conformational transitions in Na⁺-dependent HCO₃⁻ transporters. Together, these findings establish a structural framework for NCBE and offer insights into ion coupling and pharmacological modulation within the SLC4 family.

title: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K+ channel
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: To understand the process of voltage activation in Kv channels, we determined the cryo-EM structure of the Shaker channel ILT mutant (V369I, I372L, S376T), known to partially decouple the gating charge movement of the voltage sensing domain (VSD) and the opening of the pore domain (PD). The structure captures an intermediate state in which the VSD is only partially activated while the gate of the PD remains closed. Combined with computational modeling based on AlphaFold2 predictions and molecular dynamics simulations, we show that the VSD activation is transduced to the PD via a dynamic shift in the population equilibrium of the S4-S5 linker between two metastable positions, thereby providing the basis for electromechanical coupling between the two domains.

title: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Human tumor-associated microbes – the tumor microbiome – have demonstrated an increasingly important role in human health due to their relevance to cancer progression and treatment response. While the metabolism at the host-microbiota interface, such as in the human gut, has been extensively investigated in recent years, the specialized metabolites from the tumor microbiome remain uncharted territory. To address this knowledge gap, we report a survey of the biosynthetic potential of the human tumor microbiome. Utilizing high-quality microbial metagenome-assembled genomes from 3,526 human tumor tissue samples, we identify 528 biosynthetic gene clusters with the potential to encode specialized metabolites relevant to tumor pathology. We reveal that the tumor microbiome encodes known and unknown metabolites spanning multiple biosynthetic classes. From this diverse biosynthetic landscape, we express a conserved family of biosynthetic genes from the genus Fusobacterium, which has a well-established role in cancer, and discover distinct families of long-chain fatty acyl amides. We subsequently find that one of these fatty acyl amides, oleoyl γ-aminobutyric acid, has immunomodulatory and G-protein-coupled receptor partial agonist activities, potentially supporting the influence of Fusobacterium in tumor pathology. The findings of our investigation lay a foundation for further research into the roles of tumor microbe-derived metabolites in cancer.

title: Nationwide sustainability assessment of PFAS treatment in U.S. water utilities
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pose an unprecedented challenge for US drinking water systems as new national regulations mandate their removal. While granular activated carbon (GAC) and ion exchange (IX) resins are widely applied, their economic and environmental sustainability under diverse real-world conditions remains uncertain. Here we leverage a quantitative sustainable design framework (integrated techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment) to evaluate GAC and IX performance across utilities nationwide. Through uncertainty and sensitivity analyses, we identify utility size, water types (e.g., groundwater and surface water), and PFAS chain length as the dominant drivers of cost and environmental impacts. IX consistently shows lower global warming potential than GAC, though treatment of short-chain PFAS significantly increases costs. Water quality, especially total organic carbon, affects treatment performance and can change cost and environmental impacts for GAC. Results highlight disproportionate burdens on small and rural systems and the trade-offs inherent in technology selection. This work provides actionable insight for utilities and policymakers, enabling more equitable and sustainable strategies for meeting emerging PFAS standards.

title: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large repetitive elements and complex chromosomal organization continue to challenge accurate assembly of eukaryotic genomes. Optical genome mapping (OGM) provides long-range genomic information by imaging individual DNA molecules. While most OGM protocols rely on sparse enzymatic labeling that restricts resolution in poorly labeled or structurally complex regions, dense labeling strategies generate continuous fluorescence intensity profiles that offer a complementary representation of genome structure. Here we extend our Dense Optical Genome Mapping Assembly (DOGMA) pipeline, previously used for bacterial genomes, to eukaryotic genomes, exemplified by the yeasts Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe, with compact, yet structurally rich genomes. We use a competitive binding (CB)-based dense OGM protocol that produces continuous intensity profiles, reflecting local AT/GC-content, along individual DNA molecules. By explicitly accounting for structural features inherent to eukaryotic genomes that complicate assembly, DOGMA reconstructs genome-wide optical maps while avoiding collapse of non-adjacent repetitive loci. The resulting chromosome-scale assemblies span the genomes of both yeasts and show local differences relative to the corresponding reference genomes, including expanded repetitive arrays ( > 500 kbp). These results establish a comprehensive framework for scalable dense OGM to increasingly complex genomes, including the human genome, where we foresee that it can be efficiently used for disease diagnosis.

title: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plant guttation fluid provides a chemically informative readout of internal plant status, offering an externally accessible window into plant physiological processes. However, its minute volume, intermittent availability, and susceptibility to evaporation limit its use for continuous biochemical monitoring. Here we introduce PlantIonics, an integrated on-leaf microfluidic electrochemical platform for real-time, non-invasive monitoring of guttation biomarkers and leaf microenvironment. A bioinspired wedge-shaped microchannel with asymmetric wettability achieves rapid (0.6 s) and unidirectional self-driven fluid collection, providing a continuously refreshed sensing interface for dynamic guttation profiling. Combined with a multichannel sensor array and a compact wireless flexible printed circuit board, PlantIonics simultaneously measures guttation-fluid biomarkers (potassium, sodium, glucose) and local leaf microenvironment. Multi-day on-plant studies demonstrate stress-responsive guttation fluctuations that correlate with root-level ionic perturbations and light modulation, demonstrating the platform’s capability to monitor dynamic physiological regulation. PlantIonics establishes a sweat-inspired analytical framework for non-invasive plant monitoring, offering opportunities for early stress diagnostics, field phenotyping, and precision agriculture.

title: Cross-border electricity tariffs undermine power system efficiency, decarbonization and reliability in North America
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The United States and Canada share an interconnected electricity system where cross-border trade lowers costs, supports low-carbon generation and balances supply and demand during stress. Tariff disputes risk costlier or curtailed electricity imports, yet the system-wide consequences remain unclear. Here we show, using ten years of New York electricity-market data and power-system simulations, that tariffs on Canadian electricity reduce imports, raise prices, lower economic welfare and increase carbon emissions by replacing hydropower- and nuclear-rich imports with fossil-fuel generation. Tariffs above about 55% on Ontario imports, or about 90% when extended to Quebec, nearly eliminate affected imports under historical market conditions. Reduced access to Canadian power shrinks operating reserves, which provide spare capacity during unexpected shortages, increases reliance on oil-fired plants during summer peaks, and raises the risk of forced power cuts during severe winter disruptions. Open cross-border electricity trade therefore supports cost efficiency, decarbonization and grid resilience.

title: Wide-bandgap perovskite with homogeneous crystallization and suppressed halogen segregation for efficient perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The differences in crystallization and migration barriers of iodide and bromide within wide-bandgap perovskite result in inhomogeneous crystallization and halogen-phase segregation, limiting photovoltaic device performance. Here we report a sequential regulation engineering to synchronously homogenize crystallization and stabilize crystallographic phase by adding 2-iminothiolane (ITA). ITA priorly undergoes an in situ thiolation reaction with methylamine to yield a reductive 4-mercapto-N-methylformamidine (MMF). It effectively modulates perovskite crystallization toward homogenization, scavenges the detrimental molecular iodine or iodine radicals by redox reaction, and anchors the migratory iodide ions by hydrogen-bond interaction. Leveraging these contributions, the obtained perovskite films exhibit the suppressed halogen phase and enhanced ion migration barrier along the vacancy and interstitial defects-depending migration paths, achieving an efficiency of 20.45%. Moreover, the corresponding champion tandem solar cell (TSC) achieves an efficiency of 28.20% (certified 27.82%), retaining 90% initial efficiency by continuous tracking maximum power point after 700 h under ISOS-L-1 protocol.

title: High-entropy enabled two-dimensional ferroelectricity and memristive synapses in van der Waals layered materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional ferroelectric materials offer opportunities for ultrathin non-volatile electronics, but their development is limited by stringent structural requirements for intrinsic polarity. Here we show that high-entropy engineering can induce switchable polarization in centrosymmetric van der Waals materials. By introducing configurational disorder into layered metal phosphorus trisulfides, we synthesize (MnFeCoNi)1−xCdxPS3 single crystals exhibiting electric-field-induced polar states and ferroelectric-like switching at ±0.5 V, with a transition temperature up to 523 K. Combined calculations and characterizations reveal that polarization originates from electric-field-driven Cd2+ migration enabled by lattice distortions and heterogeneous coordination environments. This migration-mediated mechanism differs from conventional ferroelectric models and enables non-volatile neuromorphic functions, including long-term potentiation and bidirectional weight modulation. This work establishes high-entropy engineering as a strategy for manipulating ion migration dynamics in two-dimensional layered materials, opening a pathway toward emergent ferroelectric-like states beyond the conventional requirement of non-centrosymmetric structures.

title: Phosphorylation tunes electrostatically driven protein-RNA interactions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Phosphorylation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) regulates many biomolecular interactions, yet its quantitative effects on binding of highly charged IDPs to nucleic acids remain unclear. Here, we show that multi-site phosphorylation of the disordered arginine/serine-rich (RS) domain of the splicing factor SRSF1 functions as an electrostatic rheostat controlling RNA binding. Using enzymatic phosphorylation, phosphomimetic variants, chemically synthesized phosphopeptides, and single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer measurements, we identify the RS domain as a strong driver of protein-RNA association. Progressive phosphorylation gradually weakens this interaction, and extensive phosphorylation abolishes detectable RNA binding. Notably, the binding free energy varies linearly with RS domain net charge, independent of whether the charge arises from phosphorylation or acidic phosphomimetic substitutions. Together, our findings establish a quantitative framework for how phosphorylation tunes interactions between charged IDPs and nucleic acids, and rationalize why two acidic amino acid residues are needed to mimic the effect of a single phosphorylation event.

title: Low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe2 monolayers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The development of high-performance p-type monolayer transistors is critical for extending two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors beyond silicon in sub 1-nm technology nodes for complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits. However, insufficient doping and metal-induced gap states (MIGS) during metal deposition lead to high contact resistance, greatly limiting p-type on-state currents. Here, we demonstrate high-performance ballistic p-type monolayer tungsten diselenide (WSe2) transistors by oxygen p-doping. The controllable oxygen doping greatly reduces the number of Se vacancy defects in as-grown WSe2, and thus increases the hole mobility from 55 to 218.3 cm2 V−1 s−1—approaching the theoretical limit. Moreover, this approach also induces a heavily hole-doped contact region in p-type monolayer WSe2 devices and decreases the contact resistance from 1869 Ω·μm down to 104 Ω·μm. Consequently, a 16-nm-channel WSe2 p-type field effect transistor (pFET) delivers a saturation current of up to 1635 μA μm−1 at a drain voltage of −1.2 V and a ballistic ratio as high as 81% at room temperature.

title: Very high frequency (263 GHz) pulse EPR spectroscopy of high spin transition metal centers
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pulse Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy provides powerful tools for examining species with unpaired electrons, such as organic radicals and metal ions, in a wide variety of interesting systems. However, the lack of high power pulse amplifiers above approximately 100 GHz has limited its applicability at very high frequencies and magnetic fields. Here we describe the use of a new 10 W high frequency traveling wave vacuum tube amplifier employed in a pulse EPR spectrometer operating over a wide frequency bandwidth centered at 263 GHz. Very high frequency pulse EPR is of particular utility for studying spin S > 1/2 species, given that large broadening effects of “zero-field splitting” interactions often dominate EPR spectra obtained at low frequency. Improvements obtained at 263 GHz are illustrated for a series of high spin (S=5/2) Mn(II) complexes starting with Mn(II) impurities in a diamagnetic host up though Mn(II) bound in metal sequestering proteins. The instrument has sufficient mm-wave power to obtain high signal-to-noise electron spin echoes without a resonator, which offers a number of advantages as described herein.

title: Head-to-tail assembled borphyrins for solid-state lithium extraction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lithium is a critical mineral for advancing greener technologies. Extraction of lithium ions (Li⁺) from sea salt, minerals, and waste is important, but has been hindered by the lack of extraction methods that offer both high selectivity and strong lithium affinity. Here, we report a dioxaborole-linked, head-to-tail assembled macrocycle – termed borphyrin – featuring a rigid cavity with a 16-crown-4-like configuration. This molecule exhibits strong affinity for lithium and high selectivity over competing cations under dry solid-liquid extraction conditions, owing to its narrow binding cavity and planar macrocyclic core. Borphyrin enabled the extraction of lithium from crystalline solids of ether-insoluble salts, as well as selective extraction of Li⁺ from dried mixed-salt matrices containing alkali, alkaline earth and transition-metal salts. These results establish borphyrin as a potential molecular platform for selective lithium recognition and solid-liquid lithium extraction.

title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are considered suitable candidates for grid storage but suffer from Zn dendrites and water-induced side reactions. Incorporating appropriate hydrophobic moieties into hydrogel electrolytes is an effective strategy to reduce water activity and widen the electrochemical stability window. To further advance this molecular design framework and enable precise interphase modulation, we report a molecularly engineered zwitterionic-fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte. Within the polymer network, the rationally introduced hydrophobic fluoroalkyl moieties (–CH2CF3) strengthen hydrogen bonds between hydrophilic units and water, thereby reducing water activity and mitigating parasitic reactions. Meanwhile, the zincophilic zwitterionic units (–SO3–, –N+(CH3)3) facilitate rapid and directional Zn2+ transport, with a Zn2+ transference number of 0.76. These tailored functional groups synergistically promote the in-situ formation of an organic–inorganic solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Zn negative electrode stability, achieving over 900 h of Zn plating/stripping at 5.0 mA cm–2 and 5.0 mAh cm–2. Furthermore, Zn | |MnO2 pouch cells incorporating this electrolyte deliver a capacity of ~1 Ah and operate for over 700 h, indicating the potential of this electrolyte for large-scale energy storage applications.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Agent Fault Location Strategy in Active Distribution Network Using Synchrophasors
abstract: Locating faults and isolating the faulted sections of the network are integral to the smooth operation of any self-healing distribution system.
